tips.text: Open the closet first and pull everything onto the bed. You cannot judge how much room a visitor actually has while half of it is hidden behind a closet door, and working on the bed forces you to finish before anyone can sleep in here.

tips.label: Cleaning note
tips.text: Linen that has sat folded since spring smells of the cupboard it sat in, even though it is clean. Wash the set that goes on the bed the week a guest arrives, and open the window while you make it up.

tips.label: The trap
tips.text: Almost every object in this room arrived while you were carrying something else and had somewhere to be. That is why so little of it has ever been decided about, and why this room needs a line drawn between what belongs to a visitor and what the household has stashed here, not a tidy-up.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, deciding which sheet sets are still fit to sleep on
zones.purpose: A bed a visitor can get into tonight without you touching anything first.
zones.done_looks_like: Mattress protector on, one complete set made up on the bed, a second complete set folded inside its own pillowcase on the shelf, two pillows that spring back when you fold them in half, and nothing under the bed but one empty suitcase lying flat.

passes.sort: Take every sheet set that has been demoted to this room and try each fitted sheet on the actual mattress. If a corner pops off while you are making the bed, it is a rag, not a spare. Fold each pillow in half and let go, and anything that stays folded goes out.
passes.straighten: Nest each complete set inside one of its own pillowcases so a full change of bedding is a single grab from the shelf, and keep the spare set for this mattress size in this room rather than back in the family linen cupboard.
passes.shine: Vacuum the mattress surface and the seams with the upholstery tool, turn the mattress end to end, and wipe the top edge of the headboard, where dust settles unseen because nobody sits up in this bed.
passes.safety: Walk from the pillow to the door with the lights off, the way a guest will in the small hours in a room they do not know, and clear anything their shin will find. If the bed sits under a blind, tie the cord up out of reach of a visiting toddler.
passes.standardize: Write on a tag tucked into each bundle: bed size, one fitted, one flat, two cases, one blanket. A standard is the best way you know today, written down.
passes.sustain: Strip and wash the bed the day the guest leaves, not the day before the next one arrives, so the room sits ready rather than pending.

the_call.title: The demoted sheets
the_call.text: The linen in this room got here because it stopped being good enough for your own bed. Thin sheets, the pilled set, the flat pillows, all quietly reassigned to people who will never say anything about it. The rule that settles it: if you would not sleep on it yourself for a week, it is not guest linen, it is cleaning cloth. Keep two complete sets that pass that test and let the rest go, even if it means buying one set. Two good sets beat six tired ones, and the shelf finally holds a decision instead of a backlog.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A guest crossing an unfamiliar room in the dark to find the bathroom, with a suitcase or a footstool in the path between the bed and the door.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: A looped blind or curtain cord hanging within reach of the bed, which matters the moment a visiting family puts a small child in this room.

leave_behind.standard: Two complete guest sets, each bundled in its own pillowcase and tagged with the bed size, and one of them always on the bed.
leave_behind.trigger: When you carry the departing guest's towels to the machine, the sheets come off the bed and go in with them.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Nobody sleeps here most nights, so the enemy is settled dust and stale air, not spills. Strip it, vacuum it, turn the mattress, and work from the headboard down to the floor beneath.

surfaces.surface: The headboard top edge and front face
surfaces.method: Start high. Run a dry microfiber cloth along the top edge, where a grey band of dust builds because nobody ever sits up in this bed to disturb it. Then follow with a cloth barely damp with neutral pH multi-surface cleaner on the front face where a guest's head and hands rest, and dry it off so no film is left.

surfaces.surface: The wall side and the gap behind the bed
surfaces.method: Pull the bed a stride out from the wall. Vacuum the strip of floor and skirting that lives behind it, and run the cloth down the back of the headboard, the one face you never see when the bed is pushed back.

surfaces.surface: The mattress surface and seams
surfaces.method: Strip the bed fully. Work the upholstery tool across the whole mattress face and right into the piped seams where skin flakes and dust gather. Then turn the mattress end to end so the head end gets a rest, and vacuum the second face before you flip it back.

surfaces.surface: The made-up set and the spare set on the shelf
surfaces.method: Hot-wash the set that was on the bed and remake it. Take the second set down from the shelf, unfold it from its pillowcase, and give it a shake and an air before it goes back, because linen that has sat folded for weeks carries a shut-away smell a guest will notice the moment they turn the covers back.

surfaces.surface: The two pillows
surfaces.method: Vacuum each pillow with the upholstery tool and stand them to air while you work. Fold each one in half as you go and watch whether it springs back open on its own.

surfaces.surface: The bed frame rails, slats, and legs
surfaces.method: Dust the side rails and the exposed slats with a dry cloth, then wipe the legs and any footboard with the neutral pH cleaner where hands and vacuum heads have marked them.

surfaces.surface: Under the bed and the stored suitcase
surfaces.method: With the bed pulled out, vacuum the whole floor footprint that has been sealed off since the frame went in. Wipe the empty suitcase inside and out and leave its lid propped open a minute to air before it slides back flat.

inspect_as_you_clean: Flag a musty or shut-in smell in the spare set as you unfold it, the sign it went into storage before it was fully dry.
Flag a yellow tide line or ring on the mattress that points to a past spill, or to water tracking in from a window above the bed.
Flag a pillow that stays folded and does not spring back, and a mattress that has dipped or gone lumpy on one side.
While you turn the mattress, flag any headboard bolt or frame joint that has worked loose, and any slat that has cracked or slipped its rail.
Flag damp, rust, or a musty note on the under-bed floor or inside the stored suitcase, which tells you moisture is sitting where you never look.

zones.time_note: short, but testing the cables and the lamp switch is the part worth doing slowly
zones.purpose: The handful of things a guest needs in the middle of the night without knocking on your door.
zones.done_looks_like: A lamp whose switch you can find by feel in the dark, one charging cable per common connector plugged in and reaching the pillow, a coaster, a box of tissues at least half full, and a drawer that is genuinely empty apart from a card with the wifi name and password.

passes.sort: Open the drawer and take out what has been hiding in a room nobody uses: dead batteries, a clock radio that lost its time when the power blipped, three paperbacks nobody chose, cough drops fused into their tin. None of it belongs to a guest, and none of it belongs to you either.
passes.straighten: Set the lamp on the side a right hand reaches first from the pillow, run the charger head over the top edge of the nightstand so it hangs where a hand lands, and stand the tissue box upright rather than laying it in the drawer.
passes.shine: Wipe the lamp base and the inner rim of the shade, vacuum the drawer out rather than wiping it, and clean the water ring the last guest left because they could not find the coaster.
passes.safety: The water glass, the lamp cord and the outlet all meet in one square foot here, so run the cord behind the nightstand rather than across the top, and keep the glass on the far side from the lamp. Take your own medication out of this drawer entirely, because a visiting child opens drawers before anything else.
passes.standardize: Tape a small card inside the drawer with the wifi name and password, where the bathroom is, and which way the shower tap turns.
passes.sustain: The night before a guest arrives, switch the lamp on and plug your own phone into each cable while you make the bed, so a dead bulb or a failed cable is found by you rather than by them.

the_call.title: Two cables, tested
the_call.text: There are probably six or seven charging cables in this house that nobody can account for, and a few have drifted into this drawer on the theory that a guest might need one. They will not. A guest will find a cable, trust it because it is offered, plug in, and wake to a phone that never charged. That is worse than offering nothing. The rule: keep exactly two here, one of each connector your visitors actually carry, and prove each one tonight by charging a real device with it. Anything you cannot prove goes to the household charging drawer or into electronics recycling. An untested cable is not hospitality, it is a trap with a bow on it.

watch_for.question: Water and electricity
watch_for.text: A water glass sitting beside a lamp base and a charger head on a small surface, with the cord crossing the top where a sleepy arm sweeps it.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Your own prescriptions or painkillers left in the nightstand drawer, at exactly the height a visiting toddler explores first.

leave_behind.standard: Lamp, two proven cables, tissues, coaster, wifi card. Nothing of the household's inside the drawer.
leave_behind.trigger: When you make up the bed for an arrival, you switch the lamp on and charge your own phone from both cables before you leave the room.

shine_detail.shine_summary: This is the one square foot a guest reaches for in the dark, so it has to be genuinely clean, not just tidy. Work the lamp down to the drawer, and deal with the ring the last visitor left because they never found the coaster.

surfaces.surface: The lamp shade, base, and bulb
surfaces.method: Start at the top. Dust the outside of the shade with a dry cloth, then run a cloth around the inner rim where a grey line of dust bakes on from the heat. Wipe the base with the neutral pH cleaner, and with the lamp off and the bulb cold, wipe the bulb too, since a dusty bulb throws a dimmer, yellower light.

surfaces.surface: The top surface and the water ring
surfaces.method: Clear the top to bare and wipe it with the neutral pH cleaner. Give the pale ring left by a sweating glass a second, patient pass, working from the outside in so you do not spread it.

surfaces.surface: The coaster and tissue box
surfaces.method: Wash the coaster and dry it, and stand a fresh or topped-up tissue box back in place so a guest is not left hunting at 2 a.m.

surfaces.surface: The drawer interior and runners
surfaces.method: Take the drawer right out. Vacuum it rather than wiping, because grit drags along the base, then wipe the front edge and the runners on both sides. Wipe the wifi card and stand it back so the print faces up.

surfaces.surface: The charging cable and the sides against the wall
surfaces.method: Wipe the length of the charging cable clean of dust with a dry cloth, and run the same cloth down the lamp flex. Dust the two sides and the back panel of the nightstand where it meets the wall, and the legs and floor directly beneath.

inspect_as_you_clean: As you wipe the charging cable and the lamp flex, flag any spot where the outer sleeve is frayed, cracked, or pinched behind the leg.
Flag a water ring that has gone soft or lifted the veneer, the sign a guest's glass has been quietly soaking into the top.
Flag a lamp switch that feels loose in the hand or a bulb that flickers when you knock the shade.
Flag a drawer that catches or a runner that has come loose from its screw as you slide it back in.
Flag a sticky or musty residue in the back corner of the drawer, where a past spill was never fully cleaned out.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, because emptying two drawers means deciding where their contents actually belong
zones.purpose: Somewhere a guest can unpack, so they stop living out of a half open suitcase on the floor.
zones.done_looks_like: The top two drawers completely empty and lined, the lower drawers holding spare linens folded to one uniform footprint with a label on the inside front edge, an anti-tip strap fixed to the wall, and the dresser top carrying a lamp or a mirror and nothing else.

passes.sort: This is where the household's undecided things hide behind a closed front: off-season jumpers, a bin of cables, wrapping paper and ribbon, a bag of outgrown baby clothes waiting on a decision about a second child. The jumpers go to your own wardrobe, the cables to the drawer that already holds cables, and the baby clothes get the decision today rather than another year of storage.
passes.straighten: Put the empty drawers at the top, where a guest opens first and bends least, and the spare linens underneath, since you fetch those twice a year and they fetch socks twice a day.
passes.shine: Vacuum inside each drawer and wipe the runners, then leave the empty drawers open with the window cracked while you finish the rest of the room. Old wood holds a smell, and a guest's clothes take it on in one night.
passes.safety: A dresser with two empty top drawers is lighter at the top than it looks, and a visiting child will climb it. Strap it into a stud, and pull each drawer fully out to check that it stops rather than sliding free onto a foot.
passes.standardize: Write on a label inside each empty drawer's front edge: reserved, guest. It stops the household reading a visibly empty drawer as an invitation.
passes.sustain: During your own seasonal wardrobe change, you open these two drawers in the same trip and confirm they are still empty before the swap counts as done.

the_call.title: The overflow you told yourself was free
the_call.text: You have been storing things in here on the reasoning that the room stands empty most of the year, so the space costs nothing. It costs the whole point of the room. The rule: these two drawers belong to the guest and are never available, not for a week, not for the box you are about to sort properly, not for the winter coats until spring. When something in the house needs a home and this dresser is the only candidate, that is not a reason to take the drawer, it is a signal that you have not yet decided about the thing. Make the decision instead. This is the drawer that turns a storage room with a bed in it back into a guest room.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: An unstrapped dresser with heavy linens low and empty drawers high, in a room where a visiting child is often left to play while the adults talk downstairs.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Dry cleaning film or the plastic bags spare bedding came sealed in, left inside a low drawer a small guest can open on their own.

leave_behind.standard: Top two drawers empty and labelled reserved, lower drawers holding only spare linens for this room's bed, strap fixed to the wall.
leave_behind.trigger: When you swap your own wardrobe over between seasons, you check the guest drawers are still empty before the swap counts as finished.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Old wood holds a smell, and a guest's clothes take it on in a single night. The point of cleaning here is to air the empty drawers as much as to wipe them, so open everything and let the room breathe through it.

surfaces.surface: The dresser top and the lamp or mirror on it
surfaces.method: Dust the top first, then lift the lamp or mirror rather than wiping around it and clean the ring of dust it was hiding. Wipe the top with the neutral pH cleaner. If a mirror stands here, finish it with a streak-free glass cleaner so it does not haze in the low light of a bedside lamp.

surfaces.surface: The back edge and the wall side
surfaces.method: Reach the top back edge and the two sides against the wall, the faces that never get touched. A dry cloth lifts the settled dust, then a damp pass with the neutral pH cleaner where marks have set.

surfaces.surface: The drawer fronts and handles
surfaces.method: Wipe each drawer front, and work a corner of the cloth or a detail brush around the handles and their fixing screws where hand grease and dust collect.

surfaces.surface: The drawer interiors and liners
surfaces.method: Vacuum inside each drawer down to the base. Lift the liner, wipe under it, and set it back flat. Then leave the two empty top drawers pulled open with the window cracked while you finish the rest of the room, so the shut-away smell has somewhere to go.

surfaces.surface: The runners, the carcass, and the floor beneath
surfaces.method: Wipe both runners of every drawer so they run true, dust the sides of the carcass and the kick base, and vacuum the floor tucked underneath the front feet.

inspect_as_you_clean: Flag a musty note in the empty drawers or in the stored linens, which tells you the wood or the bedding is holding damp.
Flag small round holes or a fine powder in old wood, the trail woodworm leaves behind.
Flag a drawer that no longer runs square, a cracked runner, or veneer lifting at a front corner.
As you clear the top, flag any water stain or heat mark left by a past plant, glass, or lamp.
While you work behind it, flag an anti-tip strap that has gone slack or whose screw has started to pull from the wall.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, and the household storage is the slow part, not the hanging space
zones.purpose: Hanging space for someone else's clothes, plus whatever household storage this room has honestly agreed to carry.
zones.done_looks_like: At least a forearm's width of clear rod with six matching empty hangers on it, a clear floor square big enough for an open suitcase, household bins on the shelf in labelled lidded boxes with nothing loose above head height, and a strip of tape on the rod marking where the guest section ends.

passes.sort: Take everything out and put it on the bed. This closet is where the house keeps holiday decorations, a wedding dress in a zipped bag, a box of old phones, and paperwork from two addresses ago. Sort by whether a named person will use it in a named situation, and route the rest out.
passes.straighten: Give the guest the end of the rod nearest the door and nearest the light, put the household bins at the far end, and use matching hangers throughout so the empty six read as an offer rather than as leftovers.
passes.shine: Wipe the rod with a damp cloth, because a rod nobody touches grows a fuzz that transfers straight onto a dark shoulder, then vacuum the floor corners where dust gathers undisturbed for months.
passes.safety: Anything stored above the rod sits over the head of whoever is reaching for a hanger. Move heavy boxes down to floor level and keep only light, lidded, labelled bins on the top shelf, with nothing stacked so the top item overhangs the edge.
passes.standardize: Mark the guest boundary physically with a strip of tape on the rod or a hanger stop, so the line is visible from the doorway and does not depend on anyone remembering it.
passes.sustain: Every time you take a seasonal bin down from this closet, you check the taped line and the empty hangers before you shut the door.

the_call.title: The box you have not opened since the move
the_call.text: There are two or three boxes on that shelf that were sealed at a previous address and have travelled unopened ever since. You keep them because opening one feels like it might cost an afternoon, and you keep meaning to have that afternoon. Do it standing here, now, with one box. If you can name a specific person and a specific occasion for what is inside, it earns a labelled home. If you find yourself saying we might need it, that is not a use, that is a delayed decision wearing a use's clothes. For anything you truly cannot face, write today's date on the lid in marker and put it back. If a year passes and you have not opened it again, it leaves unopened, and you will not remember what was in it.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: Heavy boxes stored above the rod, directly over the head and hands of anyone reaching in for a hanger, in a closet nobody uses often enough to notice a bin creeping toward the shelf edge.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: Suitcases and loose bins on the closet floor, in the dark stretch of room a guest crosses barefoot on the way to the light switch.

leave_behind.standard: Six matching empty hangers past the tape line, a clear floor square for a suitcase, and every household bin lidded, labelled and below head height.
leave_behind.trigger: When you fetch or return a seasonal bin, you count the six hangers before you close the door.

shine_detail.shine_summary: A closet nobody opens for months grows a life of its own in the corners. Clean the rod so it stops marking dark shoulders, and get right into the still, undisturbed corners where dust and damp settle in.

surfaces.surface: The top shelf and the lidded storage bins
surfaces.method: Work from the top. Lift each labelled bin down, wipe the dust off its lid with a cloth barely damp with neutral pH cleaner, and dust the shelf itself before the bins go back. Check the lids sit flush so nothing settles inside.

surfaces.surface: The hanging rod and the hangers
surfaces.method: Run a damp cloth along the full length of the rod. A rod nobody touches grows a soft fuzz that transfers straight onto a dark jacket shoulder, so do not skip the ends. Wipe the six spare hangers while you are there.

surfaces.surface: The back wall and upper corners
surfaces.method: Dust the back wall and sweep the upper corners for cobwebs with the vacuum nozzle or a dry cloth wrapped on a long reach, taking in the corner where the wall meets the shelf.

surfaces.surface: The door track or hinges
surfaces.method: If the doors slide, run a detail brush or the vacuum nozzle along the bottom track to clear the grit that makes them stick. If they are hinged, wipe the hinge edges where dust cakes.

surfaces.surface: The floor, corners, and skirting
surfaces.method: Move the suitcase out and vacuum the whole floor, working the nozzle hard into the corners where dust has gathered undisturbed for months. Finish along the skirting inside the door.

inspect_as_you_clean: Flag a soft musty smell or a damp patch on the back wall, especially where the closet backs onto an outside wall that sweats.
Flag soft, buckled cardboard on a stored bin, the first sign moisture is sitting on the shelf.
As you wipe the rod, flag a bracket that is pulling from the wall or a rod that has started to bow under the weight on it.
Flag small holes in stored fabric or larvae casings in the corners, the signs of moths in a space that is opened too rarely to catch them.
Flag a closet light that does not come on, since a dark closet is one a guest cleans out of by feel.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, clearing whatever the desk has been holding for the rest of the house
zones.purpose: Where a guest lands the suitcase, charges a laptop, and answers the email they came to this room to escape.
zones.done_looks_like: A clear desk with a working lamp, a chair pulled up to it, a luggage rack or a taped floor square for the suitcase, one labelled bin holding a spare charger, wifi card, water glass, tissues and a folded spare blanket, and a reachable outlet with no cord crossing the floor.

passes.sort: Clear the surface completely. It will be holding gift wrap, an ironing pile that never made it back, a printer that has not been switched on this year, and paperwork someone brought in here to deal with in peace. The ironing goes back to the wardrobe it came from, the printer either earns a desk somewhere it gets used or leaves the house, and the paperwork goes into the file it was always headed for.
passes.straighten: Put the welcome bin where a guest sees it the moment they stand in the doorway, and set the luggage rack where a suitcase can open fully without hitting the bed frame or the closet door.
passes.shine: Wipe the desk and the chair seat and back, both of which collect a dust film in an unused room, and check the desk lamp works now rather than during a guest's first evening.
passes.safety: The classic hazard here is the extension lead run across the floor because the only outlet is behind the bed. Move the desk to the outlet rather than the outlet to the desk, and if a suitcase must live on a folding rack, open it and lean on it to be sure it holds a packed case without folding.
passes.standardize: Photograph the room in its ready state and keep the print inside the lid of the welcome bin, so setting up is matching a picture rather than remembering a list.
passes.sustain: When you carry the departing guest's sheets to the wash, the welcome bin comes with you and gets restocked on the way back.

the_call.title: The room's second job
the_call.text: Almost every guest room is also something else: the home office, the sewing room, the place the exercise bike ended up. Pretending otherwise is precisely why hosting takes an afternoon, because you are not tidying, you are relocating an entire activity under time pressure. Name the second job out loud and give it a marked footprint, then test it honestly: can you clear that footprint into one bin or one cupboard, in a single trip, without unplugging anything? If yes, share the room and set the boundary in tape. If no, the second job is too big to share this room, and something moves out for good. That decision is uncomfortable, and it is the one that turns hosting from an event into a bed change.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: An extension lead running from the desk across the open floor to the only reachable outlet, in the strip of carpet a guest walks in the dark.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: A folding luggage rack that has never been load tested, or a hard case balanced on the desk edge, in a room where a child may be playing while you carry cases in and out.

leave_behind.standard: Clear desk, marked suitcase footprint, one labelled welcome bin with the ready-state photo inside the lid, and no cord crossing a walking line.
leave_behind.trigger: When the guest's sheets go into the machine, the welcome bin is restocked and put back before you leave the room.

shine_detail.shine_summary: A guest lands a suitcase here, plugs in a laptop, and answers the email they came to this room to escape. Clean it so it works on their first evening, not so it looks good in a photo, and check the lamp comes on before they need it.

surfaces.surface: The desk lamp
surfaces.method: Dust the shade and wipe the base with the neutral pH cleaner, then switch the lamp on and off to confirm it lights now, rather than leaving a guest to find a dead bulb after dark on their first night.

surfaces.surface: The desk top and front edge
surfaces.method: Clear the desk to bare and wipe the whole top with the neutral pH cleaner, giving the front edge an extra pass where wrists and forearms leave a film.

surfaces.surface: The desk back edge, cable clip, and the space behind
surfaces.method: Reach the back edge and the cable clip, then pull the desk out enough to vacuum the dust and stray cords behind it, the gap that never gets seen.

surfaces.surface: The welcome bin and its contents
surfaces.method: Wipe out the labelled bin, wash the water glass, top up the tissues, and shake out and refold the spare blanket so it is fresh for a guest reaching for it in the night.

surfaces.surface: The chair and the luggage rack
surfaces.method: Wipe the chair seat, back, and arms with the neutral pH cleaner, or run the upholstery tool over a fabric seat, and wipe the legs. Wipe down the luggage rack and its webbing straps so a guest sets a clean case onto a clean rack.

surfaces.surface: The floor under the desk and rack
surfaces.method: Vacuum the carpet or floor under the desk and the luggage rack. On a sealed hard floor, follow with the floor-material-compatible cleaner along the guest's walking line.

inspect_as_you_clean: As you clear the desk cords, flag a plug or extension lead that feels warm, looks scorched, or has a cracked outer sleeve.
Flag a desk lamp that flickers or will not come on when you test it.
Flag frayed webbing or a loose hinge on the folding luggage rack as you wipe it down.
Flag a water ring or a heat mark on the desk top left by a past mug or laptop charger.
Flag a wobble in a desk leg or a chair joint that has worked loose under weight.

rooms.intro: A child's bedroom is the first space someone gets to run themselves, so every hook, rod and bin in here has to work at their height and their reading level rather than yours. Build it so a five year old can put the blocks away without calling down the stairs and the room mostly holds itself; build it for your reach and you will still be tidying it when they are fifteen. Start on the floor, because the floor is what everything else in this room is failing onto.

tips.label: Where to start
tips.text: Clear the floor first, working out of the Toy Storage Zone. The strip under the bed, the closet floor and the space under the desk all get much easier to judge once you can see carpet, and the room stops looking like one enormous job.

tips.label: Cleaning note
tips.text: Make Shine a two song job in here: one song for surfaces with a damp cloth, one song for picking the floor up. A child sustains what they can finish while their attention lasts, and a clean that outruns the music teaches them that cleaning never ends.

tips.label: The trap
tips.text: Doing the whole room while they are at school. It is quicker, and it costs you the point, because a child will not maintain homes they did not choose and they will notice exactly which animal went missing. Do the dull parts alone, and make every keep or go call with them standing next to you.

zones.time_note: most of it in Shine, once the mattress and the floor under the bed are stripped back
zones.purpose: The place a child winds down and sleeps, and nothing else.
zones.done_looks_like: Duvet pulled flat with one pillow squared at the head. Three or four stuffed animals on the bed, the rest sitting in an open basket at the foot where they can still be seen. Nightlight cord run behind the bed leg. A clear walkable path from the pillow to the door, wide enough to cross in the dark without looking down.

passes.sort: Pull every stuffed animal out onto the floor and count what was actually in the bed. A child sleeps with a handful, not a herd, and the rest are drift from birthdays and fair prizes.
passes.straighten: Give them bedding they can handle alone. One duvet in a washable cover beats a top sheet plus blanket plus quilt, because making the bed becomes a single pull instead of four layers a seven year old will never line up.
passes.shine: Strip the bed, vacuum the mattress, and get the strip of floor under it that nobody has seen since the frame went in. Wipe the headboard and the nightlight casing where hands land every night.
passes.safety: Blind and blackout cords hanging near a bed head are a strangle risk at exactly the wrong height. Cleat them high on the wall or change to a cordless blind. Then check the bed to door route, because a night trip to the bathroom should not end over a toy bin.
passes.standardize: Tape one photo of the made bed inside the wardrobe door at the child's eye height. Match the picture is a standard a six year old can meet on their own, with no adult needed to rule on what made means.
passes.sustain: The bed gets made while the school bag goes onto the shoulder, before anyone leaves the room. A duvet you can pull flat in one movement is the only version of this that survives a school morning.

the_call.title: The animals that never get picked
the_call.text: You already know which two or three actually get slept with. The decision you have been avoiding is not whether to thin the rest, it is whether you are allowed to do it without them. Split it: the child picks the sleepers, you handle the drift, and nothing leaves the house the same day it leaves the bed. Put the rest in a lidded box in the wardrobe for six weeks. If nobody asks for a single one, the box goes quietly. If they ask for one by name, that one comes back and the rest still go. The box is what lets you be decisive without being cruel.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Blind cords and cord loops within reach of a pillow. Cleat them above child height or fit a cordless blind.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A bag, a bin or a pile of books between the bed and the door turns a half asleep bathroom trip into a fall.

leave_behind.standard: One duvet, one pillow, and the animals that fit in two arms in a single trip. The photo inside the wardrobe door says what made looks like.
leave_behind.trigger: Bed made while the school bag goes on, every morning, before the bedroom door closes.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Shine this zone from the pillow down to the floor the frame hides. Work top to bottom, strip everything soft off first, and finish with the strip of carpet under the bed that nobody has seen since the frame went in. The thing people miss is the mattress itself.

surfaces.surface: the bedding: duvet, cover, pillow and pillowcase
surfaces.method: Strip it all first. Wash the sheet, cover and pillowcase on the hottest wash the fabric allows, and air the pillow. Remake the bed only once the mattress and frame below are done, so nothing clean goes back onto grit.

surfaces.surface: the mattress, top face and both sides
surfaces.method: Vacuum the whole top and the seams with the upholstery attachment, working the piping where skin and dust settle. Stand the mattress on edge and vacuum the underside, then flip or rotate it end to end so the same patch is not always slept on.

surfaces.surface: the headboard and the bed rails
surfaces.method: Damp cloth with a little neutral pH cleaner, top rail first because that is where hands and gums land every night, then down the uprights and along the side rails. Dry it off so no damp sits in the joints.

surfaces.surface: the nightlight casing and the shade
surfaces.method: Dry microfiber cloth over the casing to lift dust, then a barely damp cloth on the plastic. A dusty nightlight throws a dimmer, warmer light, so this is worth doing properly.

surfaces.surface: the stuffed animals and their basket
surfaces.method: Machine or hand wash the fabric ones on a gentle wash and let them dry fully before they return. Wipe any hard plastic faces or eyes with a damp cloth. Tip the basket out, vacuum the inside, and wipe the rim where small hands grab it.

surfaces.surface: the bed frame legs and the floor underneath
surfaces.method: Wipe each leg down with the neutral pH cleaner. Then pull the bed out or reach right under with the vacuum crevice tool and clear the long strip of dust and lost toys under the slats. On a hard floor, follow the vacuum with a damp mop and the floor-material-compatible cleaner.

surfaces.surface: the walkable path from the pillow to the door
surfaces.method: Vacuum the run of carpet the child crosses in the dark, or mop it with the floor-material-compatible cleaner if it is hard floor. This is the lane that has to stay clean and clear, so leave nothing drying on it.

inspect_as_you_clean: A damp patch or a musty smell in the mattress or the slats, which points to a spill or bed-wetting soaking in, or a mattress that never gets to dry. Flag it.
A slat or a frame joint that gives or creaks when you lean on it while vacuuming underneath, meaning a bolt has worked loose over months of use.
A frayed or nicked nightlight flex, or a plug that feels warm or looks discoloured, noticed while you wipe the casing.
Soft dark spots in the corner where the headboard meets an outside wall, the first sign of condensation mould.
A carpet gripper or a floorboard nail lifting proud under the bed, found the moment you reach in with the vacuum.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, because everything has to come out onto the floor before it can go back
zones.purpose: Holds the bedroom toys so a small child can put them away without asking anyone.
zones.done_looks_like: Six open bins, none higher than the child's shoulder, each with a photo of its contents taped to the front face. Blocks in one, vehicles in one, small figures in one. Enough clear carpet to lie down on. One rotation box on the wardrobe top shelf, out of reach and dated.

passes.sort: Tip every bin onto the floor and sort into families first, blocks with blocks, figures with figures. Broken toys, orphan puzzle pieces and party bag plastic go out during the sort, never into a decide later pile that becomes a seventh bin.
passes.straighten: One open bin per family and no lids anywhere. A lid is an extra step, and an extra step is the reason a five year old drops the dinosaur on the carpet instead. Heaviest bin on the bottom, the daily favourites at hand height.
passes.shine: Run the hard plastic through a sink of warm soapy water and dry it on a towel. Vacuum the skirting corners where small parts migrate, and check the bin bottoms for splits before you refill them.
passes.safety: Anything smaller than a toilet roll tube is a choking hazard for a younger sibling and belongs in a bin they cannot reach. Then check every battery hatch: button batteries are the serious one, so bin any toy whose battery cover has lost its screw.
passes.standardize: Photo label on the front face of every bin, never on a lid, at the child's eye level rather than yours. A picture of six blocks works long before reading does.
passes.sustain: Pickup happens when the bedtime story gets chosen, not after it. The story is the thing worth clearing the carpet for.

the_call.title: The set that gets tipped out and abandoned
the_call.text: Every kids' room has one: the forty small figures, or the enormous block set, that gets emptied across the carpet and walked away from before anyone has built anything. You have not thrown it out because it was expensive, or because the person who gave it asks after it. Stop deciding that on feeling and run a test instead. Half of it goes into the rotation box on the wardrobe top shelf for six weeks. When it comes back down, watch what they do with it that same afternoon. If they go straight for it and build something, it has earned a bin at floor level. If it gets tipped and abandoned again, that is your answer and the whole set moves on. Rotation, not volume, is what makes play go deep and pickup go short.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Small parts and loose button batteries reachable by a younger sibling. Anything that fits through a toilet roll tube goes up high.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: Toys left loose on the carpet between the bins and the door, which is exactly where feet go at night.

leave_behind.standard: Every toy family has one open, photo labelled bin at child height, and the carpet is clear enough to lie down on when the light goes off.
leave_behind.trigger: Floor cleared while the bedtime story is being chosen, every night.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Shine here is mostly the bins and the small parts that escape them. Work from the wardrobe top down to the skirting corners, wash the hard toys properly, and check each empty bin before you refill it. The skirting corners are where the lost pieces gather.

surfaces.surface: the rotation box on the wardrobe top shelf
surfaces.method: Wipe the lid and the shelf around it with a dry then barely damp microfiber cloth. This box is opened rarely, so it collects the fine dust that drifts up in the room.

surfaces.surface: the bin outer faces and their photo labels
surfaces.method: Wipe each front face with a damp cloth, going gently over the taped photo label so it does not peel. Sticky finger marks come off with the neutral pH cleaner.

surfaces.surface: the hard plastic toys, blocks, vehicles and figures
surfaces.method: Run them through a sink of warm soapy water, agitate to shift the grime in the seams, and spread them on a towel to dry fully before they go back in a bin.

surfaces.surface: the bins themselves, inside and bottom
surfaces.method: Empty each one completely, wipe the inside with the neutral pH cleaner, and turn it over to check the base. Dry it before refilling, since a damp bin holds a smell.

surfaces.surface: the cube unit or shelf frame the bins slot into
surfaces.method: Lift the bins out and wipe each cube opening and shelf edge with a barely damp microfiber cloth, working from the top row down. This is the frame the child grabs and leans on, so finger marks and dust build along the front edges and in the back of each empty cube.

surfaces.surface: the skirting corners and carpet edges
surfaces.method: Vacuum tight into the skirting corners and along the carpet edge with the crevice tool, because that is where small parts and dust migrate and settle out of sight.

surfaces.surface: the open floor the child plays on
surfaces.method: Vacuum the clear carpet the child lies down on. If it is a sealed hard floor, follow with a damp mop and the floor-material-compatible cleaner so knees and hands meet a clean surface.

inspect_as_you_clean: A bin bottom starting to split or a corner going brittle, found when you turn the empty bin over, which will spill the load next time it is lifted.
A cracked toy with a sharp broken edge, or flaking paint on a wooden toy, spotted as you wash and dry each piece.
A mildew smell or a dark bloom inside a bin, which means something went back in damp.
A carpet gripper or a lifting seam at the skirting, felt as the vacuum snags on it.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, and nearly all of that is paper
zones.purpose: One clear surface where homework actually gets started rather than avoided.
zones.done_looks_like: Desk surface bare except a lamp, a pen cup and one tray holding live work. Laptop charger threaded through a clip on the desk edge so the plug never drops behind the desk. Books on the shelf above, none stacked on the surface. Chair empty.

passes.sort: Paper first, and every sheet goes to exactly one of three places: live work into the tray, keepsake into the memory box, everything else into recycling. A worksheet from a finished term is recycling even when the marking was good.
passes.straighten: Pens and pencils standing in a cup within a hand's reach of the writing hand, not across the desk where a reach knocks the water bottle over. Books and folders go up onto the shelf so the surface stays a work surface.
passes.shine: Clear the whole desk down to bare wood, wipe it, then get the pencil sharpener dust and dried glue out of the drawer runners. Wipe the lamp shade too, because a dusty lamp is a dimmer lamp.
passes.safety: Count the plugs under the desk. A lamp, a laptop charger and a strip plugged into another strip is where an overloaded socket hides, so bring it back to one strip in one wall socket. Scissors and craft knives point down in the cup, and blades go in a closed drawer if a younger child comes in here.
passes.standardize: The tray is the standard: if it does not fit in the tray, it is not live work, and it goes to the shelf, the memory box or the recycling. Turn the tray out on the same evening the backpack gets emptied, so it never quietly becomes a second pile.
passes.sustain: The desk gets cleared when the laptop lid closes at the end of homework, not the next morning. Closing the lid is the trigger.

the_call.title: The finished schoolwork
the_call.text: This is the pile you keep moving instead of deciding on: exercise books, paintings, a folder of worksheets, and the flat certainty that binning any of it means you did not care. Take the judgement out of the moment and put it into a container. One memory box per child per school year, an actual box with a lid and a fixed size, kept on the wardrobe top. When it is full it is full, and the way you make room is by taking something out, not by getting a second box. Photograph the oversized art and let the paper go. Keep the pieces where you can genuinely see their hand getting better, because those are the ones worth opening in ten years. The size of the box makes the call so you do not have to make it at nine o'clock on a Tuesday.

watch_for.question: Water and electricity
watch_for.text: Chained extension strips under the desk feeding a laptop charger, a lamp and a games console. One strip, one wall socket, and keep the water bottle off the same end of the desk as the plugs.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: Craft knives and open scissors loose in a desk drawer, or standing point up in the pen cup where a hand goes in blind.

leave_behind.standard: The surface holds the current task, the lamp, the pen cup and one tray, and the tray only holds work that is still live.
leave_behind.trigger: Desk cleared to the photo the moment the laptop lid closes at the end of homework.

zones.chapter_ref: See Chapter 24, the checklist, schedule and name.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Shine the desk from the shelf above down to the cables below, and take the top right back to bare wood. The drawer runners and the cable nest under the desk are where the real grime hides, not the surface everyone sees.

surfaces.surface: the shelf above and the top edges of the books
surfaces.method: Dust the shelf board and run the cloth along the top edges of the standing books, working left to right so dust falls onto the desk you have not cleaned yet, not onto a finished surface.

surfaces.surface: the lamp shade and neck
surfaces.method: Dry microfiber cloth over the shade and down the neck. A dusty shade throws less light, so this earns its place. Wipe the switch and the base where fingers turn it on.

surfaces.surface: the laptop or tablet screen
surfaces.method: Switch it off and wipe the screen with a dry microfiber cloth only, in slow straight passes. Keep every spray and damp cloth away from it, since water and a screen do not mix. If a smear will not lift, breathe on the glass and wipe again rather than wetting it.

surfaces.surface: the desk surface, down to bare wood
surfaces.method: Clear everything off. Wipe the whole top with the neutral pH cleaner, then lift dried glue, sticker gum and marker with a dab of the degreaser on a corner of the cloth, and buff dry.

surfaces.surface: the pen cup and the live-work tray
surfaces.method: Tip the pen cup out over the bin, wipe it inside and out, and stand the pens back point down. Lift the tray, wipe under it and the ring it left, and set it back.

surfaces.surface: the drawer interior and the runners
surfaces.method: Open the drawer fully and vacuum out the pencil-sharpener shavings and dried glue that gather in the corners. Wipe the base, then run the cloth along both runners so the drawer glides and closes flush.

surfaces.surface: the chair, seat, back and casters
surfaces.method: Wipe the seat and back with the neutral pH cleaner. Tip the chair and pick hair and grit out of the casters with the detail brush so they roll clean.

surfaces.surface: the cables and power strip under the desk, and the floor
surfaces.method: Vacuum the dust off the power strip and the cable bundle with the brush tool, wipe the cables down as you handle them, then vacuum the floor under the desk where crumbs collect out of sight.

inspect_as_you_clean: A frayed, kinked or nicked laptop charger flex, or a plug and strip that feel warm or look scorched, noticed as you dust and handle the cables.
A chair caster that wobbles or a seat joint that flexes and creaks when you tip the chair to clean it.
A drawer runner cracked or bent so the drawer will not close flush even after the grit is out.
A hairline crack or a lifted patch of veneer on the desktop, uncovered once the surface is bare and wiped.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, since sizes have to be checked garment by garment
zones.purpose: Holds the clothes that fit right now, at a height the child can dress themselves from.
zones.done_looks_like: Rod lowered so the child reaches a hanger without a stool. Every hanger the same type, all facing the same way. Shirts together, dresses together, jackets together, with a hand's width gap between groups so a row can actually be read. Shoes in pairs on the floor rack, backpack on its own low hook, next size up in one labelled box on the top shelf.

passes.sort: Pull anything that is the wrong size. Children's clothes fail in one direction only, too small, so the test is quick: sleeves above the wrist bone, waistbands that leave a mark, shoes where the toe is already touching. The next size up belongs in a box on the top shelf, never mixed into the rod.
passes.straighten: Lower the rod. It is one bracket move, and it changes who is capable of using this closet. Then group by type and by colour inside each type, so getting dressed is picking from a row rather than digging through a jumble.
passes.shine: Empty the closet floor completely, vacuum it, and wipe the rod down where hangers have left a grey line. Check the top shelf for the dust that has been settling onto the stored clothes all year.
passes.safety: An overloaded rod on plastic end brackets comes down onto a child's head, so hang everything back on and give it one hard downward pull before you trust it. Heavy things, sports kit and boots and skates, live on the closet floor, never on the top shelf where a child pulls them down onto themselves.
passes.standardize: One hanger style throughout, and the next size box labelled in numbers big enough to read from the doorway. At the start of each season turn every hanger backwards, so the ones still reversed by the end of it tell you what is not being worn.
passes.sustain: The reversed hanger gets flipped forward as the garment goes back on the rod from the drying rack, so the record keeps itself and nobody has to remember anything.

the_call.title: The outgrown thing you are keeping for someone
the_call.text: A good part of what is jammed on this rod fits nobody in the house and is not going anywhere, because it is being kept for a younger sibling, a cousin, or a second child who is currently hypothetical. Make the rule concrete: name the child, and name the season they will fit it. If you cannot say both out loud, it is not being stored, it is being deferred, and deferring quietly eats the shelf you were saving. One box per next size, sealed and labelled. When the box is full, the overflow goes now rather than after one more sort. Clothes kept for nobody in particular arrive at the right size stained, dated and unworn anyway.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: An overloaded rod on plastic end brackets, or heavy sports kit and boots stored on a top shelf that a child pulls down on themselves reaching for something else.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A stool or a storage box used as a step to reach the top shelf, on a closet floor that is not clear.

leave_behind.standard: Only clothes that fit today hang on the rod, grouped by type, on one hanger style, at a height the child reaches unaided.
leave_behind.trigger: Hangers flipped forward as clothes come off the drying rack and go back on the rod.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Shine the closet top to bottom while it is emptied out: the settled dust on the top shelf, the grey line along the rod, and the floor under the shoe rack. An empty closet is the only time you can see the back wall, so look at it while you can.

surfaces.surface: the top shelf and the next-size box on it
surfaces.method: Lift the stored box down, wipe its lid, and clear the band of dust that has been settling onto it all year. Wipe the shelf board itself before anything goes back, working from the back wall forward.

surfaces.surface: the closet back wall and upper corners
surfaces.method: With the shelf clear, dust the upper corners for cobwebs and wipe the back wall, paying attention to any wall shared with the outside of the house where damp shows first.

surfaces.surface: the hanging rod
surfaces.method: Wipe the full length of the rod with a damp cloth to lift the grey line the sliding hangers leave, and dry it so hangers do not stick.

surfaces.surface: the shoulders of the hanging clothes
surfaces.method: Draw a lint brush or a slightly damp microfiber cloth over the shoulders of each garment where dust settles, working along the rod. Group by type as you rehang so the rows stay readable.

surfaces.surface: the backpack hook and the shoe floor rack
surfaces.method: Wipe the low hook and the rack shelves with the neutral pH cleaner. Knock loose grit off the rack outdoors or into the bin, since it holds more dried mud than it looks like it does.

surfaces.surface: the closet doors, both faces and the handle
surfaces.method: Wipe the outer and inner faces of the sliding or bifold doors with a damp microfiber cloth, and go over the handle and the edge where small hands push and pull it. Dry the faces so no streaks catch the light.

surfaces.surface: the closet floor and the door track
surfaces.method: Empty the floor completely, vacuum it corner to corner, then mop with the floor-material-compatible cleaner if it is a hard floor. Run the detail brush along the sliding or bifold door track to clear the grit that stops it running.

inspect_as_you_clean: A musty smell or dark specks of mould on the back wall or in the upper corners, especially on a wall shared with the outside, spotted while the shelf is clear.
A plastic rod end bracket going brittle or cracked, or a bracket screw backing out of the wall, noticed as you wipe the rod.
Moth signs, small holes or webbing, in the clothes on the rod or the stored box, found as you brush the shoulders.
A water stain or a soft patch on the closet floor, uncovered once the floor is emptied and vacuumed.

zones.time_note: most of it in Straighten, because refolding upright is the slow part
zones.purpose: Folded everyday clothes a child can get themselves dressed from without asking.
zones.done_looks_like: Five drawers, one category each, each with a picture label on the drawer front. Socks and underwear standing upright in rows so every pair is visible from above. Every drawer closes with one push, no pressing down. Dresser strapped to the wall, nothing on top of it worth climbing for.

passes.sort: One drawer at a time, tipped out onto the bed. Out go the single socks with no pair, the underwear with dead elastic, and the pyjama bottoms that now stop above the ankle. Do not open the next drawer until this one is back in.
passes.straighten: File fold upright so the drawer reads like a card index and the child sees every shirt without excavating. Dividers, or two shoebox lids, stop the rows falling sideways the first time the drawer gets yanked.
passes.shine: Pull the drawers right out of the carcass, vacuum the inside of the frame, and wipe the runners. That grit is where the drawer that sticks, and then gets slammed, comes from.
passes.safety: A chest of drawers with two drawers open is a climbing frame, and it tips forward onto the child climbing it. Strap it to a wall stud with an anti tip bracket. Then take the tablet or the toy off the dresser top, because anything a child wants up there is an invitation to climb for it.
passes.standardize: A picture label on each drawer front showing what is inside, socks on the socks drawer, so the child both finds and returns without reading. Same category in the same drawer forever, even when that means one drawer stays half empty.
passes.sustain: Refolding happens straight out of the laundry basket and into the drawer standing up, never stacked flat on the bed to be dealt with later.

the_call.title: How many shirts is enough
the_call.text: The real problem in this dresser is not folding, it is that there are eleven t-shirts in a drawer that only closes if you lean on it, and an overstuffed drawer is exactly why a child pulls the whole stack out to find one thing. Stop deciding garment by garment and set the number by arithmetic instead. Count the days between washes, add two, and that is your quantity for socks, underwear and shirts. Everything above the number goes, starting with whatever you would not choose on a normal morning. The test is mechanical, and you can run it in front of the child without an argument: if the drawer does not close with one push, you have not finished sorting.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: An unanchored chest of drawers tipping forward when the drawers are opened and climbed. Fix an anti tip strap to a wall stud and keep the dresser top bare of anything worth climbing for.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A jammed drawer that needs a hard yank, which pulls the child backwards off balance when it finally gives.

leave_behind.standard: One category per drawer, file folded upright, quantities set by the wash rhythm, and every drawer closes with a single push.
leave_behind.trigger: Clothes folded upright and put straight into the drawer as the laundry comes out of the basket.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Shine the dresser by pulling the drawers right out of the carcass and cleaning the frame inside. The grit in the runners is where a sticking, slammed drawer comes from, so this is the pass that keeps every drawer closing with one push.

surfaces.surface: the dresser top
surfaces.method: Clear it to bare, wipe the top with the neutral pH cleaner, and dry it. Nothing worth climbing for goes back up, so this stays a clean, empty surface.

surfaces.surface: the drawer fronts, picture labels and knobs
surfaces.method: Wipe each front with a damp cloth, going gently around the taped picture labels. Work the detail brush around the knobs and into the seam where the front meets the drawer box.

surfaces.surface: the drawer interiors
surfaces.method: Pull each drawer fully out, tip the lint and grit into the bin, vacuum the corners, and wipe the base. Dry it before the folded clothes go back, standing socks and underwear upright as you refill.

surfaces.surface: the carcass frame inside
surfaces.method: With the drawers out, vacuum the inside of the empty frame where dust and stray socks collect at the back, and wipe the interior shelves the drawers slide over.

surfaces.surface: the runners and tracks
surfaces.method: Vacuum each runner, then work the detail brush along it to clear the grit that jams the glide. Wipe the runner clean and check the drawer closes flush before you load it.

surfaces.surface: the sides and the floor behind the dresser
surfaces.method: Wipe the exposed sides, then vacuum the dust and lost items in the gap behind and under the dresser with the crevice tool while you have it pulled out.

inspect_as_you_clean: A cracked or bowing drawer base, or a splinter lifting on a hand-hole edge, found as you empty and wipe each drawer.
A knob or handle screw working loose, felt as you wipe around it.
An anti-tip strap gone slack or its wall screw backing out, or a drawer front rubbing because a runner is bent, noticed while the dresser is pulled out. Flag it.
A musty smell or a damp corner inside a drawer that means clothes went back not fully dry.

zones.time_note: most of it in Standardize, since the checklist is what does the real work
zones.purpose: The square metre by the bedroom door where tomorrow morning gets assembled the night before.
zones.done_looks_like: Backpack hanging on its hook at child height, packed and zipped. Shoes side by side directly underneath it. Signed forms in the front pocket rather than on the kitchen counter. Sports bag on the second hook, instrument case upright against the wall. Floor completely clear.

passes.sort: Empty the backpack completely every Friday, turned upside down. Out comes the leftover lunch, the dead permission slip and the newsletter from three weeks ago. Sports kit goes into the wash basket, never back into the bag damp.
passes.straighten: Hook, then shoes, then bag, along the wall in the order they get grabbed. The instrument case stands upright against the wall where it cannot be trodden on, and the lunchbox gets its own small hook, so an empty hook at bedtime tells you it is still in the bag with yesterday's sandwich in it.
passes.shine: Wipe the lunchbox seals and the inside of the water bottle lid, which is where the mould actually grows. Turn the backpack over a bin and shake it, then wipe the base where the drink leaked in March.
passes.safety: A bag left in a dark doorway at seven in the morning is the trip that starts the day badly, so everything hangs and nothing rests on the floor. Then check the things that must never be forgotten: an inhaler, an epipen or a dose of medication belongs in one named pocket that is checked at packing, not remembered at the school gate.
passes.standardize: A five line checklist taped beside the hook at the child's eye level, in pictures for a younger one and words for an older one. Bag, shoes, lunch, form, kit. Five lines and no more, because a longer list gets skipped.
passes.sustain: The launch zone gets packed while the bath is running, every school night, so it happens before anyone is tired enough to argue about it.

the_call.title: Who actually packs the bag
the_call.text: You have been packing it, because they are slow and you are not, and every morning proves you right. That is the decision worth reversing. Hand it over properly: the child packs against the five line list, you check the list rather than the bag, and you never silently repack it afterwards. When a form goes missing on Wednesday, the fix is a line added to the list, not you quietly doing it for them. Hold that, and remember the rule from the book. An audit checks the home, not the household. What it finds is always a system to fix, never a person to blame. It will cost you a few genuinely bad weeks, and it buys you every school morning after that.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: Bags, shoes and an instrument case left on the floor in the doorway, right in the line everyone walks at seven in the morning.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Loose medication in a backpack pocket, reachable by a younger sibling and easy to forget entirely. Keep an inhaler or epipen in one named pocket, checked when the bag is packed.

leave_behind.standard: Bag on the hook, shoes underneath, forms in the front pocket, and the five line checklist taped beside the hook at the child's eye level.
leave_behind.trigger: Bag packed and hung while the bath is running, every school night.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Shine this corner where the grime actually lives: the lunchbox seals and the water bottle lid, then the base of the backpack. Turn the bag out, wash what touches food, and finish with the small patch of floor. The bottle lid is where the mould you cannot see is growing.

surfaces.surface: the hooks and the wall behind them
surfaces.method: Wipe each hook and the wall patch behind it, where a wet bag has left a mark. Work top to bottom so drips land on floor you have yet to clean.

surfaces.surface: the backpack, base and pockets
surfaces.method: Turn it over a bin and shake out the crumbs and paper. Wipe the base with a dab of degreaser where a drink leaked and set, and turn each pocket out to clear the grit before it goes back on the hook.

surfaces.surface: the lunchbox and its seals
surfaces.method: Wash the box, and run the detail brush with a little degreaser into the seal groove and the hinge where grease and crumbs pack in. Rinse and dry fully, seal open, before it goes back.

surfaces.surface: the water bottle and its lid
surfaces.method: Scrub the lid threads and the drinking valve with the detail brush, because that is where the mould grows unseen. Rinse well and stand it open to dry, never capped wet.

surfaces.surface: the shoes underneath and the instrument or sports case
surfaces.method: Knock the grit off the shoes outdoors or into the bin and wipe the soles. Wipe down the instrument case and the sports bag, and air the sports bag if it went away damp.

surfaces.surface: the square of floor under the hooks
surfaces.method: Vacuum the patch under and around the hooks, then damp mop it with the floor-material-compatible cleaner if it is a hard floor, so the lane everyone walks at seven in the morning starts clean and clear.

inspect_as_you_clean: Mould in the water bottle valve or along the lunchbox seal, or a lingering sour smell, found as you brush and rinse them.
A hook screw working loose or pulling out of the wall, felt as you wipe the hook and hang the weight back on it.
A frayed backpack strap, a split base seam, or a broken zip pull, noticed while you turn the bag out.
A damp patch or a water stain on the floor, or a mildew smell in the sports bag, spotted as you clear and mop the corner.

rooms.intro: The nursery is the room where safety outranks everything else, and where the person using it is usually exhausted and working one-handed. Every standard here is built for that person at 2 a.m.: a bare crib, supplies inside one arm's sweep of the changing pad, cords shortened and heavy cartons moved off the shelf above the crib so nobody has to keep an eye on them. Start with the crib, because it is the quickest zone in the room and the one where getting it wrong matters most.

tips.label: Where to start
tips.text: Empty the crib before you touch anything else in the room. It is one armful of work, and the standard is a number you cannot negotiate down: one fitted sheet, and nothing else over the rail.

tips.label: Cleaning note
tips.text: Fragrance-free, infant-safe cleaners only, and crib linens on a hot wash. Wipe the changing pad after every single change rather than saving it for the weekly reset, because the pad is the surface bare skin touches most in this house.

tips.label: The trap
tips.text: Buying ahead. Diapers in the next size, clothes for next winter, a second bottle brand in case the first fails. Babies skip sizes and reject teats, and the nursery quietly fills with supplies bought for a baby who never arrived in that shape.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, because taking everything out is the whole job
zones.purpose: The one surface in the house where your baby is left alone, which is why it holds a fitted sheet and nothing more.
zones.done_looks_like: A bare mattress with one fitted sheet pulled tight to the corners, the sleep sack folded on the dresser, the monitor mounted on the wall with its cable clipped high and at least an arm's length back from the rails, and nothing draped over the top rail.

passes.sort: Lift everything out of the crib and lay it on the floor where you can see it at once: the quilt, the plush pile, the bumper, the wedge, the stack of muslins. One fitted sheet goes back in. The plush goes to the toy basket, the muslins to the changing station, the quilt to the keepsake box.
passes.straighten: Put the spares where your hand finds them in the dark. Two fitted sheets and one spare sleep sack in the top dresser drawer means a 3 a.m. sheet change is one drawer, one motion, and no ceiling light.
passes.shine: Strip and hot-wash the sheet, then wipe the mattress cover and every rail, especially the top rail where hands and gums end up. While the mattress is out, run your palm along each slat and put a spanner on the frame bolts; crib hardware works loose over months of being leaned on.
passes.safety: Drop the mattress to its lowest setting the day your baby can push up onto hands and knees, because the next thing they learn is pulling to stand. Move the crib clear of the blind cord, the lamp flex, and the monitor cable; any cord reachable from inside the rails is a strangling risk that comes down or gets shortened today. Find it, and fix it now.
passes.standardize: Photograph the empty crib with its single sheet and tape the picture inside the closet door. Anyone who puts your baby down, including a visiting grandparent, can see what the crib is supposed to look like without asking you.
passes.sustain: Every time the sheet comes off for the wash, the crib goes back together with a sheet and nothing else.

the_call.title: The quilt your mother made
the_call.text: Somebody who loves you has given you bedding for this crib. It is beautiful, it took them weeks, and it cannot go in there. The rule that settles it: sentimental bedding gets hung on the wall above the crib or folded into the keepsake box, never inside the rails, and you tell the giver once, plainly, in the same breath as showing them where you hung it. Say it early rather than letting it sit in the crib until the first time you notice it pushed up against your baby's face.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Loose bedding, bumpers, and plush in the crib are a suffocation risk to an infant who cannot roll off them, and a blind or monitor cord reachable through the slats is a strangling risk.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A mattress left at the high setting after your baby can pull to stand puts the rail below chest height, and the fall is over the side onto a hard floor.

leave_behind.standard: The crib holds a fitted sheet, a sleep sack, and your baby. Nothing else crosses the rail.
leave_behind.trigger: when you strip the sheet for the wash

shine_detail.shine_summary: This is the one surface your baby is left alone on, so clean it like you mean it and work from the mounted monitor down to the floor. Strip it bare first, because you cannot inspect a slat you cannot see.

surfaces.surface: the wall-mounted monitor, its bracket, and the clipped cable run
surfaces.method: Start high. Dust the monitor housing and its bracket with a dry microfiber cloth, then wipe the lens with a barely damp cloth so you do not smear it. Run the same cloth down the clipped cable, not to move it but to clean the dust that grows on a cord nobody touches.

surfaces.surface: the mobile hanging over the crib, if one is fitted
surfaces.method: With the crib stripped, unclip the mobile or reach it in place. Dust each arm and hanging figure with a dry cloth, then wipe the clamp and the figures with a barely damp cloth, since these are the shapes your baby stares up at and reaches for from the mattress. Let it dry fully before it goes back over the crib.

surfaces.surface: the top rail and teething rail
surfaces.method: This is where hands and gums end up, so it is a mouthing surface. Wipe it with warm water on a clean color-coded cloth first, then a light pass of neutral pH cleaner, then a second cloth wrung out in plain water to lift any residue. Let it air dry before bedding goes back.

surfaces.surface: the side rails and every slat
surfaces.method: Work slat by slat, back face and front, with a damp cloth. Draw your palm down each one as you go so you feel a rough edge or a split before you see it. Get into the corners where the rails meet the end panels, where dust and drool dry into a film.

surfaces.surface: the mattress cover and its seams and zip
surfaces.method: Lift the mattress out. Wipe the wipeable cover with neutral pH cleaner, working the piped seams and the zip channel with a corner of the cloth where crumbs and dried milk hide. Dry it fully, because a cover put back damp grows mildew underneath where you never look.

surfaces.surface: the mattress support base, frame bolts, and underside of the mattress (hidden)
surfaces.method: With the mattress out, vacuum the support board and the ledge it sits on, then wipe it. Turn the mattress and vacuum its underside too. This is the one moment you can see the frame bolts and the base, so look at them properly while they are bare.

surfaces.surface: the fitted sheet and sleep sack (the items)
surfaces.method: Strip the fitted sheet and hot-wash it, and wash the sleep sack on its label setting. Do not put either back until it is bone dry. Match the sheet tight to all four corners when it returns so nothing sits loose in the sleep space.

surfaces.surface: the floor under and behind the crib (hidden)
surfaces.method: With the crib easy to move or reach behind, vacuum the floor under it and the skirting behind it, then damp-mop or wipe the hard floor. This strip only gets cleaned when the crib is stripped, so do it now while it is open.

products_used: Washing machine on a hot wash
Baby-safe rinse or plain warm water for the mouthed rail
inspect_as_you_clean: As your palm runs down each slat, feel for a hairline crack, a splinter, or a slat that gives slightly. Flag any that move.
With the frame bolts exposed under the mattress, note any that sit proud, show a gap, or turn easily by hand, the sign the hardware has worked loose over months of leaning.
Check the clipped monitor cable along its length for a cracked or pinched section, and flag any point where it has slipped down toward the rails.
Look at the mattress cover seams and zip for a split or a soft moldy patch, and press the support base for any spot that flexes more than the rest.
Note whether the drop-side or mattress-height catches still seat firmly on both ends, and flag one that no longer clicks home.

zones.time_note: most of it in Straighten, working out what one arm can genuinely reach
zones.purpose: A pad you can work at with one hand staying on your baby the entire time.
zones.done_looks_like: Diapers, wipes, and cream all touchable without moving your feet or lifting your hand off your baby, a lined pail within one step, two spare outfits in the drawer directly beneath the pad, and a pad surface with nothing stacked on it.

passes.sort: Clear the whole dresser top. What earns its way back is only what your hand touches during an actual change: diapers, wipes, cream, a burp cloth. The lamp, the framed scan photo, and the bottle of lotion nobody has opened all move off.
passes.straighten: Stand at the pad and sweep your free arm through its full arc. Everything inside that arc is the station and everything outside it is storage. Diapers go on the side your dominant hand lands, wipes beside them, cream where your thumb can flip the cap without looking.
passes.shine: Wipe the pad after every change and pull its cover off for a hot wash weekly. Once a month take the drawer under the pad right out; that is where crusted cream lids and dried-out wipes collect underneath the spare outfits.
passes.safety: Keep one hand on your baby the whole time the strap is off, with no exception for reaching a shelf, because a roll off a dresser is a fall onto a hard floor from adult waist height. Anchor the dresser to the wall, and keep the wipe refill bags and the pail liner roll shut in a drawer rather than sitting on top where a hand can reach loose plastic.
passes.standardize: Tape a card on the wall beside the pad with the counts you restock to: eight diapers in the caddy, one wipe pack open, one sealed behind it. The card tells you the station is running low before a bare baby does.
passes.sustain: Restock the caddy back up to the numbers on the card during the last change before bed.

the_call.title: The second station downstairs
the_call.text: You have half a changing setup on the living room floor, because carrying the baby upstairs eight times a day is unbearable. The rule: run it as a full station or do not run it at all. A half-stocked spot is where you discover you have wipes and no diapers with a bare baby on a sofa. Either mirror the card exactly, same counts, same restock trigger, or replace it with a single caddy you carry down in the morning and back up at night. One and a half stations is the option that fails you.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A baby rolling off the changing pad while you turn to reach a shelf, which is why nothing needed during a change may sit outside your arm's sweep.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Loose wipe refill bags and the diaper pail liner roll left on the dresser top are thin plastic within reach of small hands, and diaper cream tubes are a swallowing risk once your baby can grab the surface edge.

leave_behind.standard: Everything you touch during a change is reachable with your feet planted and one hand on your baby.
leave_behind.trigger: at the last change before bed

shine_detail.shine_summary: A one-handed job means everything you touch should be wipeable and everything hidden should get pulled out. Wipe the pad after every change, then work the shelf, the pad, and the drawer beneath in one monthly pass.

surfaces.surface: the shelf or organizer above the pad holding diapers, wipes, and cream
surfaces.method: Take the diapers, wipes tub, and cream off and set them in the caddy. Dust the shelf, then wipe it with neutral pH cleaner, getting the ring the cream tub leaves and the film the wipes lid leaves behind.

surfaces.surface: the wall behind and beside the pad
surfaces.method: Wipe the wall at splash height with a damp cloth and a little neutral pH cleaner, because changes throw more onto the wall than you would think. Dry it so nothing beads and runs down behind the dresser.

surfaces.surface: the changing pad surface, its contour seams, and the safety strap
surfaces.method: Wipe the whole pad after every single change. On the monthly pass, wipe into the contour seams where wipe solution and cream pool, and run the cloth along the safety strap and through the buckle where grime sits in the webbing.

surfaces.surface: the pad cover (the soft item)
surfaces.method: Pull the cover off weekly and hot-wash it. Have the spare on before the wet one is off so the pad is never left bare and uncovered. Dry it fully before it goes back on.

surfaces.surface: the dresser top around the pad
surfaces.method: Clear the surface and wipe the whole top with neutral pH cleaner, working around the base of the pad and into the back edge against the wall where dust and loose wipes gather.

surfaces.surface: the drawer beneath the pad and its runners (hidden)
surfaces.method: Once a month pull the drawer right out. Tip out the sock lint, crusted cream lids, and dried-out wipes that collect under the spare outfits. Vacuum the empty cavity, wipe the drawer base and both runners, then refill and check it closes flush.

surfaces.surface: the lined pail and its lid seal
surfaces.method: Take the liner out, wipe the pail inside and out, and clean into the lid seal and hinge where odor and a soft film build up. Dry it before a fresh liner goes in.

products_used: Washing machine on a hot wash
inspect_as_you_clean: As you wipe the pad, look for a split or crack in the vinyl and a lifting seam, both of which trap moisture and bacteria under the surface. Flag it.
Run the strap through your fingers and note any frayed webbing or a buckle that no longer clicks firmly shut.
With the drawer out, note any runner screw that has backed out or a drawer front pulling away from the box.
Feel whether the dresser rocks at all against the wall as you lean on it, and flag a wobble.
Check the pail lid seal for a soft moldy line in the rubber and flag it.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, and the sorting is the part that costs you something
zones.purpose: Holds the sizes your baby fits this month and moves everything else out of the house fast.
