This is where the household's rejected products retire: the shampoo nobody liked, the body wash that smells wrong, the conditioner welded to the shelf. Keep one shampoo, one conditioner, one body wash, all readable and more than a third full. The rest go, along with the old razor and the disintegrating loofah.
passes.straighten: Hang the caddy or fit a corner shelf so nothing stands directly on the tub floor collecting water underneath it. A bar of soap gets a draining dish, never a puddle. Put a hook inside the door at a height someone can reach with wet hands and no glasses on.
passes.shine: Start with the mold, because it needs time you should not spend standing there: spray the grout lines and the bottom band of the curtain liner, go clean the rest of the room, then come back and rinse. A fabric liner goes in the washing machine rather than getting scrubbed by hand.
passes.safety: Fall: your guest is stepping into an unfamiliar tub, probably at night, on a surface they cannot judge the grip of. Put a non-slip mat or adhesive strips on the tub floor and make sure there is one thing solidly anchored to grab, because a towel bar screwed into drywall will tear straight out the moment it takes a person's weight.
passes.standardize: Three bottles, one soap, one mat, one anchored grab point, and no personal items. If the shower has stood unused for a month, run it hot for a minute before a guest arrives, which clears the stale water sitting in the line and proves the drain is still running freely.
passes.sustain: Whoever used it last squeegees the glass or shakes out the liner and drapes the bath mat over the tub rim. A liner left bunched against the tile is exactly where the pink film starts again.

the_call.title: The grout you cannot clean
the_call.text: You have scrubbed one grout line three times, it stayed gray, and you have quietly started calling that clean. It is not dirt. It is mold that has grown into porous grout or a silicone bead that has failed underneath, and no product will bring it back, so every week you spend part of the clean on a job that cannot succeed. The rule: give a stained line one proper treatment with full dwell time and a stiff brush. If it darkens again within two weeks, stop cleaning it and move it to the repair list, which means raking out and regrouting, or cutting out the old silicone and running a fresh bead. Calling it a repair is the decision. It is a Saturday afternoon once, instead of a chore forever.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: An unfamiliar tub with a slick glazed floor, used at night by someone who does not know the room. A non-slip mat or strips are the fix, not a warning.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: A towel bar or a suction rail being used as a grab handle. Both let go under load, and the person comes down against the tub rim on the way.

leave_behind.standard: One shampoo, one conditioner, one body wash, all readable and above a third full, over a non-slip tub floor.
leave_behind.trigger: When you strip the guest bed after a visit, carry out whatever the guest left in the shower on the same trip to the laundry.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Start the mold clock before anything else: spray the grout lines and the bottom band of the liner, then walk away and clean the rest of the room while it works. Come back to rinse, and finish at the tub floor and the apron where the last of the water sits.

surfaces.surface: the ceiling above the shower and the exhaust vent grille
surfaces.method: Look up first. Wipe the ceiling above the shower and the vent grille with a dry cloth to clear dust, then a cloth dampened with soap-film cleaner over any speckled spots. This is the highest and most humid surface, so it comes before you wet the walls below it.

surfaces.surface: the grout lines and the silicone corners
surfaces.method: This is your dwell job. Spray the soap-film cleaner along the grout lines and into the silicone corners, and if the film there is stubborn switch to a dedicated mildew remover. Leave it to sit while you clean the rest of the room, then come back, work it with a stiff grout brush, and rinse thoroughly so nothing is left biting the grout.

surfaces.surface: the shower head, the arm, and the wall tile
surfaces.method: Wipe the head and arm with soap-film cleaner to shift the scale, then work the wall tile top to bottom, spraying and wiping in bands so the runoff always lands on tile you have not cleaned yet. Rinse the whole wall down at the end.

surfaces.surface: the bottle caddy or shelf and the three bottles
surfaces.method: Lift the caddy or clear the shelf, wipe the sticky rings under each bottle, and wipe the caddy or shelf itself. Wipe each bottle neck, and stand them back once they are dry.

surfaces.surface: the curtain liner or the glass screen and its track
surfaces.method: Send a fabric liner straight to the washing machine rather than scrubbing it by hand. A plastic liner or a glass screen gets soap-film cleaner over its face and along the bottom edge where the pink film starts, then a rinse. Wipe the rod or the screen track, and wipe the screen dry so it does not spot.

surfaces.surface: the taps, the spout, the diverter, and the tub surround
surfaces.method: Wipe the surround from the back wall forward, then bring the taps, spout, and diverter up with soap-film cleaner, working the scale off the handles and the base of each fitting. Rinse and buff the metal dry so it shines.

surfaces.surface: the tub floor, the non-slip surface, the drain, and the rim
surfaces.method: Clean the tub floor last, working the non-slip surface with soap-film cleaner and the grout brush since the grip texture holds grime. Clear the drain and stopper, rinse the whole tub from the rim down, then wipe the rim and hang the bath mat over it to dry rather than leaving it on the floor.

surfaces.surface: the tub apron or side panel down to the floor line
surfaces.method: Wipe the apron or side panel from the top down to where it meets the floor, and run the cloth along that floor joint where splash collects and lingers. Dry the joint so no standing water is left against the tile.

products_used: Dedicated mildew remover (not in this zone's list, for grout the soap-film cleaner will not shift)
Stiff grout or detail brush (not in this zone's list, and the grout and the non-slip floor need bristles)
inspect_as_you_clean: Pink or black film that returns in the same grout lines within days, the sign that moisture is sitting there and not drying.
The silicone bead at the tub-to-wall joint peeling, blackening, or lifting at an edge.
Grout that feels soft or crumbles under the brush, or a wall tile that shifts when you press it.
Scale crusting the shower head so the spray splits and sprays sideways.
A brown bloom or a spreading stain on the ceiling above, which points to something wet in the floor above or the roof.

zones.time_note: quick throughout, though Shine wants dwell time under the rim before you do anything else
zones.purpose: It has to be clean and stocked in a way that is obvious to someone who will never ask you where anything is.
zones.done_looks_like: One spare roll standing in plain sight on the tank or in a holder a seated person can reach without standing up. A brush that is dry, resting in a holder with no liquid pooled in the bottom. A small trash can with a liner actually in it. No ring at the water line, and a dry, dust-free floor behind the pedestal.

passes.sort: Clear everything from the top of the tank and the floor behind the bowl: the collection of air fresheners, the second brush, the magazines, the box of something nobody has identified in years. One reserve roll stays in the open. Nothing else.
passes.straighten: Put the reserve roll where a seated person can reach it without getting up, since that is the entire point of a reserve roll. Set the brush and the trash can on the side away from the door swing so nobody kicks either one on the way in.
passes.shine: Treat the bowl first and let it sit under the rim and at the water line while you work outward: seat hinges, then the base of the pedestal, then the floor behind it, which is where splash and dust collect and where the smell in a guest bathroom actually comes from. Use a cloth in a color you use nowhere else in the house.
passes.safety: Poison, choke, or strangle: a bottle of bowl cleaner parked behind the pedestal sits at a crawling child's eye level, usually with the cap loose. It goes back in the cleaning bin with the cap tight every time. It never shares a shelf with bleach, because bleach and an acid bowl cleaner mixed in a small room with the door shut produce a gas that will drop a healthy adult.
passes.standardize: One visible reserve roll, backstock in the cabinet, brush dry in its holder, liner in the can, no ring at the water line. Write those five lines on a card and stand it in the cleaning bin, so the person holding the brush reads the standard at the moment they are able to meet it.
passes.sustain: When you carry the trash out on collection night, you are already standing here, so drop in a new liner and check that the reserve roll is still upright.

the_call.title: The brush nobody wants to touch
the_call.text: The toilet brush in a guest bathroom is the object your household has silently agreed not to look at. It has splayed bristles, it stands in an inch of gray water in the bottom of its holder, and it has been there for years, spreading more than it removes. The decision you are avoiding is that a brush is a consumable, not a fixture. The rule: splayed bristles or liquid in the holder means both go out today and a fresh set comes in, and from then on the brush gets rinsed in the flush and left propped under the closed seat to drip before it goes back in the holder. If that much handling is more than you will realistically do, buy the kind with a disposable head and stop negotiating with yourself about it.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Bleach and an acid bowl or limescale cleaner used one after the other in a small room with the door closed and no fan running. Use one product, ventilate, and never store the two together.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: A bowl cleaner bottle left standing behind the pedestal after cleaning. It is at floor level, in reach, and the cap is rarely back on properly.

leave_behind.standard: One reserve roll visible from the seat, a dry brush in a dry holder, a lined can, and no ring at the water line.
leave_behind.trigger: Trash collection night is liner night in here, and the reserve roll gets checked while you are holding the bag.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Treat the bowl first and let it work under the rim and at the water line while you clean outward: seat, then pedestal, then the floor behind it, which is where the smell in a guest bathroom actually lives. Use a cloth in a color you use nowhere else in the house.

surfaces.surface: the inside of the bowl, under the rim and at the water line
surfaces.method: Start here so it can dwell. Run bowl cleaner around under the rim and let it sheet down over the water line, then leave it while you work everything outward. Come back with the bowl brush, scrub under the rim and around the ring, and flush.

surfaces.surface: the wall behind and above the tank
surfaces.method: While the bowl sits, wipe the wall behind and above the tank with neutral pH cleaner, top down, since splash and dust reach higher here than you would think. Dry it off.

surfaces.surface: the tank lid, the top, and the flush handle
surfaces.method: Wipe the tank lid and top with neutral pH cleaner, and give the flush handle a proper wipe on every face, because it is the one thing in the room every guest touches. Dry the handle.

surfaces.surface: the tank sides, the supply line, and the shutoff valve
surfaces.method: Wipe down the tank sides, then follow the supply line to the shutoff valve at the wall and wipe along it. Dry as you go so you can tell fresh cleaner from anything that is wet on its own.

surfaces.surface: the seat top, the underside, and the hinge bolts
surfaces.method: Wipe the seat top, then lift it and clean the underside and the bowl rim it sits on, which is the part most often missed. Work the soap-film cleaner into the hinge bolts and the crevices around them, then dry.

surfaces.surface: the bowl exterior, the pedestal base, and the floor bolt caps
surfaces.method: Work down the outside of the bowl and the pedestal with soap-film cleaner, paying attention to the tight curve where the base meets the floor and to the bolt caps. Rinse and dry.

surfaces.surface: the floor behind the pedestal, the trash can, and the brush holder
surfaces.method: Finish at the floor behind and beside the pedestal, the spot the smell comes from. Vacuum the dust first, then wipe the floor with neutral pH cleaner. Empty and wipe the trash can and drop in a fresh liner, and rinse the brush holder so no liquid pools in its bottom.

products_used: Toilet bowl cleaner and a dedicated bowl brush (not in this zone's list, and the bowl needs both)
inspect_as_you_clean: Water pooling or a stain creeping out at the base of the pedestal where it meets the floor, a sign the seal beneath is passing.
Rust or damp on the supply line and the shutoff valve behind the tank.
Beads of condensation sweating down the outside of the tank and reaching the floor.
A seat that rocks on loose bolts, or a hairline crack running out from a bolt hole in the tank or the bowl.
The mineral ring at the water line coming back fast, the mark of hard water and a slow, weak flush.

zones.time_note: the hands-on part is short; the wash cycle you started at the beginning of the room is what sets the pace
zones.purpose: It holds one complete fresh set of towels so hosting never starts with a search.
zones.done_looks_like: One bundle per expected guest, each holding a bath towel, a hand towel, and a washcloth folded together, matching in color, smelling of nothing at all. A clean bath mat folded flat beneath the bundles. A hand's width of air above the stack. No thin gray towel kept for the dog sharing the shelf.

passes.sort: Unfold every towel and look at it in daylight rather than closet light. Anything thin along the fold line, permanently gray, stiff from too much softener, or carrying a hair dye or nosebleed stain comes out of the guest stack. It becomes a rag or a car towel today. It does not go back just in case.
passes.straighten: Store as complete sets rather than in stacks of like with like. Bath towel, hand towel, and washcloth folded into a single bundle so setting up for a visitor is one lift instead of three searches. Two bundles ready covers most households, and the bath mat lives underneath them.
passes.shine: Wash the stored set hot even though nobody has used it, because a towel that has sat folded in a closed closet all season carries a musty note that appears the instant it gets wet. Wipe the shelf, then run your hand along the back wall of the closet, since damp there is what the towels have been drinking.
passes.safety: Burn or fire: if this closet also holds the water heater, towels pressed against the tank, a hot pipe, or the heater's cable are a scorch and fire risk that no amount of neat folding fixes. Leave a hand's width of clearance around anything that gets hot, and never let a stack lean on the unit or trap its cable behind it.
passes.standardize: Two complete bundles on the marked shelf with the bath mat beneath, and a mark on the shelf edge showing where the second bundle ends. When one is missing, the gap reads as a gap without anyone counting.
passes.sustain: When a guest leaves and you strip the bed, the used bathroom set goes straight into that same wash, and the shelf gets restocked before the sheets are dry.

the_call.title: The good towels
the_call.text: Every house has a set of nice towels that guests are not quite allowed to use and a set of worn ones that guests actually get, and nobody ever says this out loud. Towels thin whether they are used or not, so holding the good ones back means they will age untouched in a closet while your visitors dry off on something gray. The rule: the guest bundle is built from the best towels you own, put into service today, and the ones they replace get demoted to rags on the same trip so they cannot creep back. And if a towel is genuinely too good for a guest to use, then it is not linen, it is a keepsake, and it belongs anywhere except the towel shelf.

watch_for.question: Burn or fire
watch_for.text: Textiles stacked against a water heater, a hot pipe, or its power cable in a shared closet. Keep a hand's width of clear air on every hot side.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A bath mat with a curled or hardened rubber backing. It stops gripping the tile and slides out from under someone stepping off wet.

leave_behind.standard: Two complete bundles, bath towel plus hand towel plus washcloth in each, and the bath mat folded beneath.
leave_behind.trigger: The guest's departure is the trigger: strip the bed and the bathroom together, wash them together, restock the shelf before you sit down.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Wash the stored set hot even though nobody has touched it, because a towel that has sat folded all season carries a musty note that shows up the instant it gets wet. While the shelves are bare, run your hand along the back wall, since damp there is what the towels have been drinking.

surfaces.surface: the top of the closet and the top shelf edge
surfaces.method: Start high and dry. Run the vacuum brush along the very top of the closet and the top shelf edge, which is where this room's dust actually settles and where nobody looks, then wipe the edge with a barely damp cloth.

surfaces.surface: the shelves and their front lips
surfaces.method: With the shelves cleared, wipe each one from the back forward with neutral pH cleaner, including the front lip where hands grip to pull a stack out. Dry each shelf fully before anything goes back, because linens go musty from a shelf that returned damp.

surfaces.surface: the back wall of the closet
surfaces.method: Wipe the back wall with a dry cloth first so you can feel it, then a lightly damp one over any marks. Dry it off. This is less about grime and more about reading the wall while you have it clear.

surfaces.surface: the linen bundles and the bath mat
surfaces.method: Send the whole stored set and the bath mat to the washing machine on a hot wash, then refold each bundle as a bath towel, hand towel, and washcloth together once they are fully dry. A hand's width of air stays above the finished stack.

surfaces.surface: the door interior, the track, and the hinges
surfaces.method: Wipe the inside of the door and the handle with neutral pH cleaner, and vacuum then wipe the track or the hinges where dust builds. Dry the handle.

surfaces.surface: the closet floor, and the water heater or pipes if they share the space
surfaces.method: Vacuum the floor and the corners, then wipe the closet floor with neutral pH cleaner, working from the back out to the threshold. If the water heater or its pipes share this closet, dust them down with a dry cloth only and keep water and damp cloths well away from them.

products_used: Washing machine (not a listed product, but the stored linens need a hot wash)
inspect_as_you_clean: A cool, damp, or musty back wall, the sign moisture is coming through from outside or from a pipe run behind it.
A water stain or a bloom of mildew on a shelf board or on the closet ceiling.
Rust, scorch marks, or condensation on the water heater and its pipes where they share this closet.
A shelf bracket beginning to pull away from the wall under the weight, or a bath mat whose rubber backing has gone hard and stopped gripping.

rooms.intro: Laundry is the one job in the house that arrives dirty, sits wet, and only counts as finished when it is back in a drawer, and it can stall at any of those points. It almost always stalls at the folding counter, but the fix starts two zones upstream at the machines, because a washer you have to empty before you can fill is what makes a household skip the last step. Start at the washer and dryer, get them clean, clear and safe, and the rest of the room unblocks behind them.

tips.label: Where to start
tips.text: Both machines first. Empty the drums, clear the lids, then pull the dryer out and look at what is behind it. Every other zone in this room is waiting on those two machines being ready to take a load.

tips.label: Cleaning note
tips.text: Lint screen every load, and once a month lift the folds of the washer door gasket and pull the detergent drawer right out to wash in the sink. Wipe the gasket dry and leave the washer door ajar between loads so the rubber is never sitting wet.

tips.label: The trap
tips.text: Clean laundry with nowhere to go. If the folding counter is still holding yesterday's basket, the problem is not the counter and it is not the folding. Nobody has been named to carry the clothes out of the room, so the dry load goes back in for a second tumble.

zones.time_note: most of it behind the machines, where the duct and the fill hoses live
zones.purpose: Run loads reliably, and stay maintained well enough that the machines are never the reason laundry stops.
zones.done_looks_like: Both drums empty with the washer door propped ajar, nothing at all sitting on either lid, a clean lint screen back in its slot, and a strip of masking tape on the side of the dryer with the month you last cleared the duct written on it.

passes.sort: Clear the tops of both machines and the inside of both drums. The single sock behind the agitator, the hardened box of dryer sheets, the bottle of softener you stopped using: all of it comes off the machines now rather than being shuffled sideways.
passes.straighten: Machine lids carry nothing. Put the vent brush and the pack of machine cleaner tablets on the shelf above, so the lids open freely and a knocked cap cannot roll down behind the drum where nobody retrieves it.
passes.shine: Lift the folds of the door gasket and wipe out the coins, hairpins, and grey slime that collect in there. Wash the detergent drawer in the sink, then run a hot cycle with a cleaner tablet in the empty drum.
passes.safety: Clear the lint screen every single load, then check the duct behind the dryer for the soft grey packing that builds where the pipe bends. Lint plus heat is a fire, and a crushed foil accordion duct traps far more of it than a smooth rigid pipe does.
passes.standardize: Write the month on masking tape stuck to the side of the dryer each time you clear the duct, so the next check is a glance instead of an argument with your memory. A standard is the best way you know today, written down.
passes.sustain: When the dryer buzzer sounds, the lint screen gets cleared before the door closes again. That one motion, every load, is the whole machine standard.

the_call.title: The duct you have not looked at
the_call.text: You have been telling yourself the dryer just runs a bit slow these days, and that towels have always needed two cycles. The dryer is not slow, it is blocked. The rule: if you cannot name the month you last pulled the machine out and cleared the duct, that is today's job, no debate. And while the dryer is already out and the duct is disconnected, look at what it is made of. If it is the flexible foil accordion kind, replace it with rigid metal now rather than promising yourself you will do it next time, because there is rarely a next time. Once a year is a cheap habit, and the failure it prevents burns the room it happens in.

watch_for.question: Burn or fire
watch_for.text: Lint packed in the duct behind the dryer, and lint on the heating element side of the screen housing. This is the highest heat and the most fuel in any indoor room outside the kitchen.

watch_for.question: Water and electricity
watch_for.text: Rubber fill hoses that have gone hard or bulged at the collar, sitting a hand's width from a wall outlet. A split hose sprays under pressure and does not stop until you reach the tap.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: A machine that walks across the floor on an unbalanced spin because a foot is not level, and the sharp sheet metal edge underneath when you tilt it back to check.

leave_behind.standard: Both drums empty, washer door ajar, lint screen cleared, before you leave the room.
leave_behind.trigger: when the dryer buzzer sounds and you are still standing next to it

shine_detail.shine_summary: Two machines that look clean hide their dirt in three places: the gasket folds, the detergent drawer, and the drum itself. Work top down, save the gasket and the lint screen for last, and finish with a hot empty cycle.

surfaces.surface: The tops and lids of both machines
surfaces.method: Clear everything off first. Mist neutral pH cleaner onto a microfiber cloth rather than onto the machine, wipe from the back edge forward, then buff dry with a second cloth so no film is left where the next basket lands.

surfaces.surface: The control panel, dials, and door handles
surfaces.method: Go over the buttons and dials with a dry cloth to lift lint, then a barely damp microfiber over the handle and the panel where hands leave grime. Keep water out of the dial seams and work a small detail brush into the ridges where grime has set.

surfaces.surface: The detergent drawer and its cavity
surfaces.method: Pull the drawer out to its stop and lift it free. Wash it in the sink in warm water to shift the caked powder and the blue softener gel, scrub the siphon cap with the detail brush, and wipe inside the empty cavity where black mould films the roof of it before you slide it back.

surfaces.surface: The washer door gasket folds and glass
surfaces.method: Peel back each fold of the rubber boot and wipe out the coins, hairpins, and grey slime, working right around the seal. Wipe the inside of the glass where detergent scum clouds it, dry the folds so they do not sit wet, then prop the door ajar so the drum breathes.

surfaces.surface: The washer drum interior
surfaces.method: Wipe the drum with a damp cloth, then run the longest, hottest cycle empty with a washer drum cleaning tablet, or the machine's own clean setting, to clear the biofilm your cloth cannot reach.

surfaces.surface: The dryer lint screen and its housing
surfaces.method: Pull the screen and peel the lint mat off it. If dryer sheets have left a waxy film, wash the mesh under running water and dry it fully. Vacuum inside the empty slot with the crevice tool before the screen goes back.

surfaces.surface: The dryer drum and its door
surfaces.method: Wipe the dryer drum with a barely damp microfiber to lift the fabric softener film and stray lint, then dry it. Clean the inside of the door and its seal where lint packs into the lip, and leave the door open afterward so the drum airs.

surfaces.surface: Behind and underneath the machines, and the floor
surfaces.method: Ease the machines out on their feet, vacuum the dust and lint drift off the back panel and the slab, and wipe the skirting and the floor where damp collects.

inspect_as_you_clean: A water stain or damp ring on the floor under the washer that dries and comes back points to a slow leak at a hose collar or the pump seal. Mark it and note the date.
Rust bleeding from under the detergent drawer or around the drum lip is the enamel giving way. Flag it before it stains the next white load.
A musty smell that survives a hot clean cycle means biofilm deeper than the drum reaches. Note it.
A scorch mark or a warm brown patch on the dryer cabinet, or a power cord that feels stiff or looks scuffed near the plug. Flag any of these.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, squinting at labels on bottles you have not opened since last winter
zones.purpose: Hold the chemistry that actually gets used, at a dose you can measure and out of a child's reach.
zones.done_looks_like: One working detergent, one bleach, one tub of oxygen powder and one stain treatment standing on a wipeable tray, the pod tub latched and above shoulder height, the true dose line inked on the cap, and not one unlabeled bottle on the shelf.

passes.sort: Line every bottle, stick, spray and pod tub up on the floor. Anything crusted shut at the neck, anything with the label washed off, and anything bought for one stain that already came out goes to the disposal pile. Two open jugs of the same detergent become one jug in use and one refill.
passes.straighten: The everyday detergent and its dosing cap sit within arm's reach of the open washer lid, because that is where you use them. Bleach and the stain sprays go behind them on a tray, and the pod tub goes higher than a child can reach on tiptoe from an upturned laundry basket.
passes.shine: Detergent drips, always. Wipe the spigot on the jug and the shelf under it, then stand every container on a shallow tray so the next drip lands on plastic you can rinse rather than a shelf that stays tacky for a year.
passes.safety: Bleach and any ammonia based cleaner never share a shelf, and never share a bucket. The pod tub gets a latched lid or a high shelf without exception, because a detergent pod looks exactly like a sweet to a toddler and bursts in the mouth.
passes.standardize: Mark the true dose line on the cap with a permanent marker, since the moulded cap is bigger than the dose almost every time. Write the job on the tray edge under each bottle, wash, whites, stains, so a returned bottle lands back in its own footprint.
passes.sustain: When you pour the last dose out of a jug, the empty goes straight to recycling and the replacement goes on the shopping list before you press start on that load.

the_call.title: The five half used stain removers
the_call.text: Every laundry shelf has them: a box of dye grabbing sheets, two spray bottles, a stick that dried solid in the cap, and something a relative swore by. You keep them because binning a mostly full bottle feels wasteful, so instead they sit there being wasteful slowly. The rule: keep the one treatment you have personally watched lift a stain, plus a tub of oxygen powder, which handles most of what the others promise. Everything else leaves today. A treatment you do not trust enough to reach for first is not a supply, it is a decision you have been postponing, and it is holding the one arm's reach of shelf next to the open washer lid.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Detergent pods within a child's reach, and bleach stored next to an ammonia based cleaner where a spill can mix the two into a gas in a small room with the door shut.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: A full jug of detergent stored above head height. Wet hands, a smooth handle, and a shelf you reach into blind is how a heavy bottle lands on a face.

leave_behind.standard: One product per job, standing on a tray, with the real dose line marked on the cap.
leave_behind.trigger: when a jug runs empty and you are holding it

shine_detail.shine_summary: Everything here drips, so the shelf under a weeping spigot is the real job. Wipe from the pod tub above down to the tray, and stand every container on plastic you can rinse.

surfaces.surface: The high shelf and the latched pod tub above shoulder height
surfaces.method: Dust the shelf top with a dry cloth, then wipe the outside of the pod tub and the shelf lip with a damp microfiber. Keep the lid shut so no water reaches the pods.

surfaces.surface: The container exteriors and their caps
surfaces.method: Wipe each bottle from the shoulder down, paying attention to the detergent spigot and the crusted cap threads where dried powder cakes. Run a detail brush around the measuring cap's fill line so you can still read the true dose.

surfaces.surface: The shelf the containers stand on
surfaces.method: Lift every container off, mist neutral pH cleaner onto the cloth, and wipe the whole shelf, working the set drips and the sticky softener rings. Dry it before anything returns.

surfaces.surface: The wipeable drip tray
surfaces.method: Carry the tray to the sink, rinse it, scrub the tacky corners, dry it, and set it back so the next drip lands on plastic you can rinse rather than a shelf that stays tacky for a year.

surfaces.surface: The shelf underside, edge, and bracket
surfaces.method: Wipe the underside and the bracket where bleach fumes and stray drips work on the metal, and clear the front edge where drips run down.

surfaces.surface: The floor beneath the shelf
surfaces.method: Vacuum any spilled powder first, then wipe the floor with the floor-material-compatible cleaner where a bleach splash has marked it.

inspect_as_you_clean: A crystallized crust building where a spigot weeps tells you that jug drips every single use. Flag the drip, not just the crust.
Rust rings or a corroding shelf bracket under the bleach are the fumes eating the metal. Note them.
A pod that has swollen, sweated, or split inside the tub. Flag it.
A container whose label has worn or bleached until you cannot read it. Flag it as unnamed.

zones.time_note: most of it deciding how many sorting streams your household will genuinely honour
zones.purpose: Turn dirty clothes into loads that can go straight into the machine without being handled twice.
zones.done_looks_like: Three labeled bags standing clear of the walking line, each below half full, a small dish on the shelf holding nothing older than today, and bare floor in front of the washer door.

passes.sort: Empty every hamper and see what a real week actually produces: whites, darks, towels, delicates, work clothes. Any stream that never fills on its own gets merged into another, and the spare hampers you were holding for those streams leave the room.
passes.straighten: One bag per stream, standing where clothes are actually taken off rather than where the bags happen to fit. Add a small dish on the shelf for pocket contents, because coins, hair ties and the occasional memory stick need somewhere to land that is not the drum.
passes.shine: Damp gym kit is what makes a hamper smell, not dirt. Wipe the inside of each bin while it is empty, and never let a wet towel spend the night in a lined bag with the lid down.
passes.safety: A hamper parked on a landing or at the top of a step is a fall you take with your arms full and your view blocked. Keep the bags out of the walking line entirely, and never carry a basket loaded higher than your eyeline.
passes.standardize: Label each bag with the load it makes rather than the colour it holds: hot towels, cold darks, gentle. Anyone in the house can then start a machine without asking which setting the bag wants.
passes.sustain: Pockets get checked as the item goes into the bag, not later at the machine. That dish on the shelf is where a lip balm stops being a whole ruined load.

the_call.title: The delicates bag that never fills
the_call.text: You sort into five streams because a care label once told you to, and one of those bags has been sitting a third full for three weeks while the thing you actually wanted washed waits inside it. The rule: a stream earns its own bag only if it has run as a full load, by itself, in the last month. Everything that fails that test merges into cold and gentle with a mesh bag inside the drum. Sorting is only worth doing when it produces a load you can run today, and a bag that waits three weeks is not sorting, it is a small pile of clothes you have taken out of circulation.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: A hamper standing in the walking line between the door and the machines, or resting on a stair tread while you go back for the rest.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: Reaching blind into a bag of work clothes where a utility knife, a razor blade or a pocketful of screws came home in a trouser pocket.

leave_behind.standard: Every bag is a load, labeled by wash setting, and emptied before it passes half full.
leave_behind.trigger: when you undress at the end of the day

shine_detail.shine_summary: Damp gym kit is what makes a hamper smell, not dirt. Wipe every bin out while it is empty, clear the walking line, and never let a wet towel spend the night in a lined bag with the lid down.

surfaces.surface: The shelf and its small dish
surfaces.method: Empty the dish, wipe the shelf with a damp microfiber, and clear anything sitting there older than today.

surfaces.surface: The three sorting bags, inside and out
surfaces.method: Tip each bag empty, vacuum the crumbs and grit from the bottom seam, wipe the inside walls with neutral pH cleaner on a cloth, and wipe the outside where hands grab it. Let each one air fully before it lines up again.

surfaces.surface: The washable bag liners
surfaces.method: Pull any washable liner out and launder it, because that is what actually holds the smell. Dry it right through before it goes back in the bag.

surfaces.surface: The lids, rims, and the frame the bags stand in
surfaces.method: Wipe the lid rims and the frame or stand where damp and lint settle unseen, and dry them off.

surfaces.surface: The walking-line floor in front of the washer
surfaces.method: Vacuum the strip of bare floor between the door and the machines, then mop it with the floor-material-compatible cleaner so no detergent film leaves it slick.

inspect_as_you_clean: Soft dark spotting or a musty note in a bag seam is mould starting in the weave. Flag it.
A liner that has torn, or a bag bottom that has gone soft and damp. Note it.
A frayed carry strap or handle on a bag you haul up the stairs loaded. Flag it before it lets go.
The small dish holding a button battery, a coin, or a screw that rode in on a pocket. Flag it.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, clearing off everything that was parked here and never collected
zones.purpose: Turn a finished dry load into clothes that are back in drawers the same day.
zones.done_looks_like: A counter bare enough to roll pastry on, one empty basket per bedroom stacked underneath it, six spare hangers on the rail at the end, and no clean clothing anywhere in the room.

passes.sort: Clear the counter right down, including everything that was never laundry: the post, the toolbox, the parcel waiting to be returned, the vase from Christmas. Whatever is parked here is the reason a dry load goes back in for a second tumble.
passes.straighten: Keep one basket per person or per bedroom under the counter, so folding and delivering are the same motion rather than two separate jobs. Hangers live on a rail at the end, not in a tangled heap you have to unpick before you can use one.
passes.shine: Wipe the counter before you fold, not after. Clean clothes pick up whatever detergent dust and lint the last load shed here, and a folding board skates badly over grit.
passes.safety: If you iron on this counter, the iron gets one heatproof rest and the cord runs behind it where no arm can hook through. When you step away, unplug at the wall rather than trusting the switch or the auto shutoff.
passes.standardize: The counter is either completely empty or holding exactly one load in progress. There is no third state. Photograph it empty and tape the photo inside the cupboard door so nobody has to guess what clear means.
passes.sustain: Tip the basket out onto the counter rather than setting it down full. A full basket on the floor keeps its clothes for another day, while a heap on the counter gets dealt with before anyone can use the surface again.

the_call.title: The single sock box
the_call.text: You are keeping a growing bag of unmatched socks because tomorrow the partner might surface. Occasionally one does, which is exactly why the bag never gets thrown out, and meanwhile it has become a permanent tenant on the one surface in this room that has to stay clear. The rule: singles get one shoebox and nothing larger. When the box is full, or at the change of season, whichever arrives first, everything still unmatched becomes a cleaning rag or leaves the house. A sock that has waited a whole season is not going to be reunited. It is just going to keep charging you the counter, and the counter is where the whole room jams.

watch_for.question: Burn or fire
watch_for.text: An iron left face down or resting on its cord on the folding counter, with clean clothing stacked within reach of the soleplate.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: Baskets stacked high on the counter, and any wall cupboard above it loaded with heavy backstock over the spot where you stand and lean in to fold.

leave_behind.standard: The counter is bare or holding one load, and every basket under it is empty before bed.
leave_behind.trigger: when you tip a dry basket out onto the counter

zones.chapter_ref: See Chapter 25, the ideal state photo.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Wipe the counter before you fold, not after, because clean clothes pick up whatever detergent dust and lint the last load shed here. Work from the cupboard above down to the floor.

surfaces.surface: The wall cupboard above the counter
surfaces.method: Open it and wipe the interior shelves and the spare detergent stock stored there, then wipe the door fronts and the top edge with a damp cloth, and dust the very top of the cupboard where lint settles and nobody looks.

surfaces.surface: The counter top
surfaces.method: Clear it bare and lift any folding board off. Mist neutral pH cleaner onto the cloth and wipe the whole run. Where an iron or a warm basket has left a starchy or greasy film, take a second pass with the food-area degreaser and buff dry so the board does not skate on grit.

surfaces.surface: The counter front edge and underside lip
surfaces.method: Wipe the front edge and the underside where you grip and lean in to fold, which collects more grime than the top does.

surfaces.surface: The baskets stacked underneath
surfaces.method: Pull each basket out, vacuum the lint and stray socks from the bottom, wipe the rims, and stack them back one per bedroom.

surfaces.surface: The hanger rail at the end
surfaces.method: Wipe the rail and the hooks of the six spare hangers where dust greys them.

surfaces.surface: The floor at your standing spot
surfaces.method: Vacuum the lint drift and any dropped pegs, then wipe the floor so nothing underfoot moves while your arms are full.

inspect_as_you_clean: A scorch mark or a heat-blistered patch on the counter from the iron soleplate. Flag it.
A loose screw or a bracket starting to pull on the wall cupboard above where you lean in. Note it.
The iron cord scuffed, kinked, or gone stiff near the plug. Flag it.
A water stain or soft swelling on the underside of the counter, or a wobble in its legs. Note it.

zones.time_note: most of it deciding what truly cannot go in the drum
zones.purpose: Dry the few things a hot drum would ruin, and get them off the rack the moment they are dry.
zones.done_looks_like: The rack folded flat against the wall with dry bars, its drip tray wiped out and empty, the rail holding six spare hangers, and nothing hanging that was washed before today.

passes.sort: Strip the rack completely. Anything still damp goes back on, anything dry goes to its drawer right now, and the wool jumper that has been draped over the end rung since spring either goes away properly or leaves the house.
passes.straighten: The rack gets one spot with a drip tray underneath, not wherever the last load abandoned it. Hang bras, wool and swimwear on the top rungs where air actually moves, and keep the bottom rungs for flat items that can take the slower dry.
passes.shine: A rack that is stored damp grows a musty smell and passes it straight to the next load hung on it. Wipe the bars dry when you strip it, and fold it flat so both faces get air rather than pressing wet metal against wet metal.
passes.safety: Water on a hard floor under a drying rack is a slip you take in socks with an armful of laundry. Keep the drip tray in place, and never stand the rack where drips can reach a wall outlet or a plugged in extension lead running along the skirting.
passes.standardize: The rack is either in use holding one set of damp items, or folded flat against the wall. Nothing has permanent residence on the rungs, and no garment starts a second night up there without a reason you could say out loud.
passes.sustain: Before you open the washer to start the next load, you clear the rack. Anything dry comes off first, which means the rack is always ready for the load you are about to run.

the_call.title: The garment that only ever hangs
the_call.text: There is at least one thing on that rack you have washed more times than you have worn. It is hand wash only, it takes two days to give up its water, and it holds the rack hostage the entire time while everything else waits its turn. The rule: think back to the last three times it was washed and name the occasion you wore it for each one. If you cannot name all three, the garment is charging you rack space and drying days it has not earned, and it goes. Line dry only is a real running cost, not a neutral care label, and it should only ever be paid for clothes you genuinely reach for.

watch_for.question: Water and electricity
watch_for.text: A drying rack standing over a wall outlet or across an extension lead, with garments dripping onto the floor beneath them.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: The wet patch under the rack on a hard laundry floor, walked over in socks by someone carrying a basket they cannot see past.

leave_behind.standard: The rack is in use or folded flat, never left standing half loaded.
leave_behind.trigger: when you open the washer to start the next load

shine_detail.shine_summary: A rack put away damp grows a musty smell and hands it straight to the next load hung on it. Wipe the bars dry, empty the tray, and fold it flat so both faces get air.

surfaces.surface: The top bars and rails of the rack
surfaces.method: Strip it bare, wipe each bar with a damp microfiber to lift the film clothes leave behind, then dry it with a second cloth before you fold it away.

surfaces.surface: The rungs and folding joints
surfaces.method: Wipe down into the joints and pivots where water sits after a load, and dry them so they neither seize nor spot with rust.

surfaces.surface: The drip tray
surfaces.method: Carry the tray out, rinse it, scrub the corners where mould starts, dry it, and set it back level under the rack.

surfaces.surface: The clip hangers used for drip-drying
surfaces.method: Wipe the clip hangers and their pegs where wet garments hang and drip, working off the chalky lime spots the drying water leaves, then dry them so they do not mark the next shirt.

surfaces.surface: The wall and floor beneath the rack
surfaces.method: Wipe the skirting behind the rack for splash marks, then mop the floor under it with the floor-material-compatible cleaner so the wet patch does not stay slick.

inspect_as_you_clean: Rust blooming at the rack's joints and folding pivots, where water pools and never fully dries. Flag it.
Black mould speckling the tray corners, or a bar that still smells musty after you have wiped it. Note it.
A hinge or lock gone loose, or a bar that no longer holds its angle when you set it. Flag it.
A water stain spreading on the wall or skirting behind the rack. Note it.

zones.time_note: most of it in Straighten, getting handles off the floor and onto the wall
zones.purpose: Hold the tools that keep this room and the strip of floor in front of the machines clean, dry and ready.
zones.done_looks_like: Broom, mop and dustpan hanging heads up with painted outlines showing behind each one, a single labeled caddy holding every vacuum attachment, a mop head that is dry to the touch, and the bucket sitting inside its taped floor square with nothing stored inside it.

passes.sort: Stand every tool up in the open: the broom, the mop, the dustpan, the vacuum hose and its attachments, the sack of rags. Two brooms become one broom. The crevice tool that fits no vacuum you still own goes out today.
passes.straighten: Hang the broom, mop and dustpan on a wall rail with the heads uppermost and clear of the floor, because bristles resting on concrete splay and then re-soil the floor they touch. Vacuum attachments live in one labeled caddy, so a missing one is visible rather than assumed.
passes.shine: Rinse the mop head and hang it to dry before it goes back on the rail, and empty the vacuum canister before you store it. A mop put away wet and grey spreads that water back down the next floor it touches.
passes.safety: A broom handle leaned against the wall behind a door swings and falls at head height the moment the door opens. Everything is hung or in a bin, nothing leans. Drain cleaner and bleach in this corner sit on a shelf above the mop bucket, never inside it where a rinse could mix them.
passes.standardize: Paint or tape an outline behind each hook so a missing tool shows from the doorway, and give the bucket a taped square of floor that belongs to it alone. The room then reports its own state without anyone opening a cupboard.
passes.sustain: When you clear the lint screen at the end of a wash day, sweep the strip of floor in front of the machines with the broom that is already hanging an arm's length away.

the_call.title: The rag pile
the_call.text: Worn towels, holed T-shirts and a retired set of sheets have quietly become a rag supply large enough to clean a small hotel. It grows because turning a worn item into a rag feels like thrift rather than a decision, so nothing is ever really discarded, only reclassified. The rule: rags live in one bin and only one bin, and nothing new becomes a rag until something old leaves as waste. If you cannot work through one bin of rags in a year, you are not saving cloth, you are storing it in the room with the least spare space. The same rule settles the second vacuum you are keeping for the garage: if it has not run in a year, it is not a spare, it is a broken machine with an excuse.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: Long handled tools leaned against a wall or stored behind a door, ready to swing down at head height when the door moves.

watch_for.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
watch_for.text: Drain cleaner and bleach kept at floor level next to the mop bucket, where they get knocked, decanted, or mixed during a rinse.

leave_behind.standard: Nothing leans, nothing stores wet, and every hook has an outline behind it.
leave_behind.trigger: when you clear the lint screen at the end of a wash day

shine_detail.shine_summary: The tools that clean the room have to be clean and dry themselves. Rinse the mop, empty the vacuum, and put nothing back wet or grey.

surfaces.surface: The hanging broom and dustpan
surfaces.method: Take each off its hook. Knock the broom out over the bin, then pull the wound hair and lint off the dustpan lip and its brush. Wipe both handles down where hands leave grime, and hang them heads up again.

surfaces.surface: The wall hooks and the painted outlines behind them
surfaces.method: Wipe the hooks and the outlined wall with a damp cloth so the painted shapes stay crisp and you can still see at a glance what is missing.

surfaces.surface: The caddy of vacuum attachments
surfaces.method: Tip the attachments out, clear the hair wound around the brush tool and the crevice nozzle, wipe each one, and empty the vacuum canister before the caddy goes back.

surfaces.surface: The mop head
surfaces.method: Rinse it until the water runs clear, wring it hard, and hang it to dry before it returns to the rail, so it does not spread grey water down the next floor it touches.

surfaces.surface: The bucket and its taped floor square
surfaces.method: Rinse and dry the bucket inside and out, wipe the taped outline on the floor so its edges still read, and set the bucket back empty inside the square.

surfaces.surface: The chemical shelf above the bucket
surfaces.method: Wipe the bottle exteriors and the shelf where drain cleaner and bleach weep, keeping the cloth off the labels so they stay readable.

surfaces.surface: The floor of the corner
surfaces.method: Vacuum the dust and lint from the corner, then mop it with the floor-material-compatible cleaner.

inspect_as_you_clean: A mop head still slimy or sour after rinsing, or a broom head shedding its bristles. Flag them.
A cracked bucket, a split broom or mop handle, or a dustpan edge gone rusty. Note it.
The vacuum cord scuffed or stiff near the plug, or a canister seal that no longer closes cleanly. Flag it.
A weeping drain cleaner or bleach bottle, and the shelf bracket beneath it corroding or loosening under the weight. Note it.

rooms.intro: This is the room where physical clutter and unmade decisions about paper live in the same drawer. Almost nothing here is heavy or dirty, which is exactly why it sits untouched for years: every item asks for a judgment rather than a lift. Start with the desk surface, because you need one finished workspace to sort everything else onto, and give the file drawer a morning of its own.

tips.label: Where to start
tips.text: Clear the desk surface completely before you open a single drawer. Every other zone in this room gets emptied onto that surface at some point, so it has to be the first thing finished and the last thing you let refill.

tips.label: Cleaning note
tips.text: Everything in here is either electronics or paper, so a wet cloth is the risk. Power devices down first, spray screen cleaner onto the cloth and never onto a screen or the scanner glass, and use a dry cloth for toner dust, because water turns loose toner into ink.

tips.label: The trap
tips.text: This is the room with a door that closes, so it quietly becomes the household's holding pen: the broken lamp, the unopened box from the last move, the bag of things with nowhere else to go. Anything that is not office work has to walk out today, or it becomes permanent furniture.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, because every item you lift off the surface needs a decision before it goes back
zones.purpose: One clear surface for the work you are actually doing right now.
zones.done_looks_like: The monitor, keyboard, and mouse in fixed positions, one notebook, one inbox tray holding fewer than a dozen sheets, no sticky notes on the monitor bezel, and the power strip hooked off the floor so the chair rolls over bare carpet.

passes.sort: Take everything off the surface and onto the floor, then put back only what the task in front of you needs, plus the inbox tray. The dead pens, the second mug, and the fringe of sticky notes around the screen do not go back up.
passes.straighten: Keyboard square in front of the monitor, notebook on your writing-hand side, phone face down beyond it, and the whole sweep the mouse travels left bare so you are never steering around a stapler.
passes.shine: Power down, wipe the screen with cleaner sprayed onto the microfiber cloth, then do the desk edge and the underside lip where your forearms rest, which is the grubbiest part of the whole room.
passes.safety: Lift the power strip off the floor onto a hook on the desk leg, and check that no charging cable crosses the arc the chair rolls through. Your feet should find nothing under there.
passes.standardize: Photograph the cleared desk and tape the print inside the top drawer, so the word clear stops being a matter of opinion in this household.
passes.sustain: When you shut the laptop lid at the end of the working day, reset the surface to match the photo before you stand up. Doing it next morning is too late, because by then the pile has been sitting there since last night and reads as normal.

the_call.title: The half-finished thing
the_call.text: One corner of the desk is held by a project you have not touched in weeks and cannot put away, because putting it away feels like admitting it is over. Say the next physical action out loud in one sentence. If you can name it ("call the insurer", "sign page four"), it is live: write that sentence on a card, clip it to the papers, and it goes in the inbox tray, not on the desk. If you cannot name a next action, it is not stalled, it is abandoned. Box it, write today's date on the lid, put it on the shelf, and if the box is still unopened on that date next year, it leaves unopened.

watch_for.question: Water and electricity
watch_for.text: A mug of coffee sitting behind the keyboard on the same surface as a power strip and a laptop charger. Move drinks to the far side of the mouse, away from cables and the machine.

watch_for.question: Fall
watch_for.text: Charger cables and the power strip lead running across the floor where the chair moves and where you push back to stand.

leave_behind.standard: The desk holds the tools of the current task plus one inbox tray, and nothing else stays there overnight.
leave_behind.trigger: When you close the laptop lid for the day.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Power down first, then clean top to bottom and back to front, screen to floor. The two spots that hold the most grime are the ones you touch most: the screen and the underside lip where your forearms rest all day.

surfaces.surface: The monitor screen and bezel
surfaces.method: With the screen off and cool, spray a screen-safe cleaner onto a dry microfiber cloth, never onto the glass, and wipe in one direction so no drips run down into the seam. Use a second dry cloth to buff. Run a dry corner along the bezel groove where dust and skin flakes pack in.

surfaces.surface: The keyboard and the gaps between the keys
surfaces.method: Turn it upside down and give it a shake, then run the vacuum crevice tool along the rows to lift crumbs and hair from between the keys. Wipe the key tops with a barely damp microfiber cloth and neutral pH cleaner, wringing it almost dry so no liquid runs under the keys.

surfaces.surface: The mouse and its underside
surfaces.method: Wipe the body and the wheel with a barely damp cloth, then flip it and clean the sensor window and the feet pads with a dry corner, because built-up fuzz there is what makes the pointer skip.

surfaces.surface: The task lamp: shade, arm, and base
surfaces.method: Only once the bulb is cool, wipe the shade or head, the arm, and the base with a barely damp microfiber cloth. Lift the baked-on dust off the top of the shade where the heat sets it, and keep the cloth clear of the bulb and the switch so no damp reaches the wiring.

surfaces.surface: The desk top, its front edge, and the underside lip
surfaces.method: Clear the surface, spray neutral pH cleaner onto the cloth and wipe the whole top, then do the front edge and reach under to the lip where your forearms rest. That underside is the grubbiest part of the whole room, so give it a firm pass and a dry buff after.

surfaces.surface: The power strip, cables, and cable tray
surfaces.method: With everything still powered down, wipe dust off the top of the strip where it hooks on the desk leg and run a dry cloth down each cable and along the cable tray. Do not wet the strip or the plugs, a dry cloth only around anything electrical.

surfaces.surface: The chair: seat, armrests, and casters
surfaces.method: Vacuum the seat and back with the upholstery tool to lift dust from the weave, wipe the armrests where hands and sleeves land, then tip the chair and pick hair and thread out of each caster by hand so it rolls clean.

surfaces.surface: The carpet or floor in the arc the chair rolls through
surfaces.method: Move the chair aside and vacuum the whole roll zone under and around the desk, getting right into the corner where the strip hooks up. Finish on bare floor with a floor-safe pass if it is sealed.

inspect_as_you_clean: As you handle each cable, look for a charger lead that has frayed or split at the plug end, and flag it.
Feel the power strip as you dust it and flag a warm body or a browned, discolored socket.
When you wipe the underside lip, push gently up and side to side and flag any joint or bracket that has started to work loose.
Check the chair casters as you clear them: one that no longer swivels or a cracked wheel is worth flagging before it seizes mid-roll.

zones.time_note: quick once you commit, though the cable and charger sorting eats more of it than you expect
zones.purpose: Hold the small tools you reach for without looking, and the live files you touch weekly.
zones.done_looks_like: A top drawer with a divided tray holding pens that all write, one stapler, one pair of scissors point-down in its own slot, and a deep pedestal drawer of hanging files with tabs all standing in one line.

passes.sort: Tip the top drawer onto the cleared desk and test every pen on scrap paper. Dried highlighters, bent paperclips, loose staples, dead batteries, and chargers whose device you cannot point at in this house all go now.
passes.straighten: Daily hand tools live in the divided tray up top, hanging files fill the deep pedestal drawer, and the two never mix. The stapler does not end up riding on the folders, and no folder gets laid flat across the pens.
passes.shine: Vacuum the drawer bottoms, which collect eraser crumbs, loose staples, and paperclip fuzz, then wipe the runners so the drawer closes without a shove.
passes.safety: Scissors and the letter opener get their own slot with points facing the back of the drawer, because you reach into this drawer blind while looking at the screen.
passes.standardize: Write what each drawer front holds, in the words this house actually uses, so tape and stamps are found without pulling three drawers.
passes.sustain: When you sit down to pay the household bills, put back into the drawers anything that migrated out onto the desk that week.

the_call.title: The cable bag
the_call.text: Somewhere in the pedestal there is a bag or a drawer of cables, adapters, and wall bricks, and it survives because each individual cable is too cheap to think about and too specific to throw away. That decision cannot be made one cable at a time. Empty the whole lot onto the desk at once, pick up each cable, name the device it powers, and point at where that device physically is in this house. No device, no keep. Then keep exactly one spare of each connector type you still use daily, coil and band it, and take the rest to electronics recycling this week. Made in one batch at the cleared desk, it is a single sitting. Made one cable at a time, it never gets made at all.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: Loose scissors and a letter opener rolling free in a drawer you reach into without looking, and a pedestal that tips forward if you pull the loaded file drawer fully out while the top drawer is open.

leave_behind.standard: One purpose per drawer, every pen in it writes, and the scissors live point-down in a fixed slot.
leave_behind.trigger: When you sit down to pay the bills.

shine_detail.shine_summary: The mess in a desk drawer hides under the divider and in the runner track, not on top. Lift the tray right out, clear the grit that jams the slide, and the drawer will close with a fingertip again.

surfaces.surface: The divided pen tray and its slots
surfaces.method: Lift the whole tray out and tip it over the bin, then run the small detail brush along each slot to sweep out eraser crumbs and dried ink. Wipe it with a barely damp microfiber cloth and let it dry before it goes back.

surfaces.surface: The top drawer bottom and corners
surfaces.method: With the tray out, vacuum the drawer bottom and get the crevice tool right into the back corners where loose staples and paperclip fuzz collect. Wipe the base with neutral pH cleaner on a wrung-out cloth and dry it.

surfaces.surface: The drawer runners and slide track
surfaces.method: Brush the grit out of both runner tracks with the detail brush, then wipe each runner clean and dry. Slide the drawer a few times to confirm it moves without a shove before you refill it.

surfaces.surface: The deep pedestal file drawer and its hanging rails
surfaces.method: Lift the hanging folders out in a block, vacuum the drawer floor, and wipe the two side rails the folders hang from. Check the base is fully dry before the files return, since paper wicks any leftover damp.

surfaces.surface: The drawer fronts, pulls, and pedestal sides
surfaces.method: Wipe the fronts and the handles where fingers grip, then run a cloth down the outside sides and the top of the pedestal where dust settles unseen against the desk.

surfaces.surface: The floor and casters under a rolling pedestal
surfaces.method: Roll the pedestal clear, vacuum the patch of floor it sat on, and clear hair from its casters by hand so it tracks straight when you push it back.

inspect_as_you_clean: As the drawer slides on its clean runner, flag any grinding or a drawer that no longer closes flush, since that points to a bent runner or a loose fixing.
Look at the runner metal for rust bloom or a bent lip and flag it rather than forcing the drawer past it.
Smell the deep file drawer while it is empty: a musty note means damp is reaching the paper, so flag it.
Check the drawer pulls as you wipe them and flag a screw that has backed out or a handle that has gone loose in your hand.

zones.time_note: nearly all of it in Sort, and it is hundreds of small keep-or-shred calls in a row, so start it fresh rather than at the end of a session
zones.purpose: Keep the documents you are genuinely required to hold, and put your hand on any one of them without opening a second drawer.
zones.done_looks_like: Hanging folders labelled by the question you would ask when looking, tabs all in the same position so your eye runs one straight line, a closed fireproof box holding the permanent originals, and a full shred bag by the door ready to go.

passes.sort: Work one drawer at a time into three piles: keep as paper, scan then shred, shred now. Tax paper by year, warranties and manuals only for machines still in this house, and no folder for anything the issuer will reprint on request.
passes.straighten: File by the question you will ask when you go hunting, so "car", "house", "health", "school", rather than by document type. Nobody has ever gone looking for a folder called Correspondence.
passes.shine: Filing is where you inspect: check the drawer bottom for damp, look for silverfish, and photograph any thermal receipt that has started to fade before the print disappears entirely.
passes.safety: Get the permanent originals out of a cardboard box on top of the cabinet and into a closed fireproof box at floor level, and keep the paper mass away from the power strip and any heater.
passes.standardize: Write your retention rule on a card and tape it inside the top drawer, naming which categories are permanent, which run by tax year, and which get scanned. A standard is the best way you know today, written down.
passes.sustain: When the new tax paperwork arrives each year, that is the signal to pull and shred the oldest year that has passed your retention period. One in, one out, and the drawer never overflows again.

the_call.title: What you are actually required to keep
the_call.text: Most of this drawer is neither obviously permanent nor obviously rubbish, and that middle band is why the whole job stalls. Split it into three by rule. Permanent originals, meaning birth and marriage certificates, deeds, vehicle titles, wills, and immigration papers, go into one closed fireproof box and never into the filing cabinet. Tax returns and their supporting paper get one folder per year and are held for whatever your local retention period is, which you look up once and write on the card. Everything else, the bank statements, the utility bills, the receipts for things you no longer own, goes by this test: if the issuer will reprint it on request, or it already lives inside an online account, it is information, not a record, and information does not get a folder.

watch_for.question: Burn or fire
watch_for.text: A four-drawer cabinet of dense paper standing against a heater, or the overflow boxes stacked on top of a power strip. Paper is the fuel load of this room, so keep it clear of heat and of the outlet.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: A tall filing cabinet will tip forward onto you if the top drawer is loaded and pulled fully out. Anchor it to the wall and open one drawer at a time.

zones.chapter_ref: See Chapter 24, the checklist, the schedule, and the name.

leave_behind.standard: Every folder is named for the question you would ask when looking for it, and the retention card taped inside the drawer decides what stays.
leave_behind.trigger: When next year's tax paperwork lands on the desk.

shine_detail.shine_summary: This is the zone where cleaning and inspecting are the same job. You cannot check a drawer bottom for damp or a receipt for fading without emptying the drawer, so clean it and read it at the same time.

surfaces.surface: The top of the cabinet
surfaces.method: Clear whatever has landed up there, then wipe the top with neutral pH cleaner on a cloth. Dust falls heaviest here and it drifts down into the open drawers, so start high.

surfaces.surface: The drawer interiors and drawer bottoms
surfaces.method: Working one drawer at a time, lift the folders out, vacuum the drawer floor and back corners, then wipe the bottom with a wrung-out cloth and let it dry fully before the paper goes back.

surfaces.surface: The hanging folder rails
surfaces.method: Wipe both side rails the folders ride on, and run the cloth along the runner track so the drawer glides. A rail with grit on it drags every folder you pull.

surfaces.surface: The cabinet front, drawer faces, and handles
surfaces.method: Wipe the drawer faces and the pull handles where hands mark them, then do the sides of the cabinet. A dry buff afterwards stops streaks on a painted steel front.

surfaces.surface: The fireproof box holding the permanent originals
surfaces.method: Wipe the outer shell and the lid seam with a barely damp cloth, keeping water away from the seal, and clear dust from the hinge so the lid still closes flush.

surfaces.surface: The floor under and behind the cabinet
surfaces.method: Ease the cabinet out if it moves, or use the crevice tool to reach behind and beneath, and vacuum the dust and any silverfish that shelter in that dark gap.

inspect_as_you_clean: Check each drawer bottom as you empty it and flag any damp patch or cupped, softened base that says water is getting in.
Watch for silverfish and their droppings in the corners and behind the cabinet, and note it as a pest sign.
As you handle the files, flag any thermal receipt whose print has begun to gray and fade, so a copy can be made before it disappears.
Give the cabinet a gentle push while it is empty and flag a rock or a lean that means it is not sitting square on the floor.

zones.time_note: most of it in Sort, and it goes faster if you take everything off the shelves in one go rather than shelf by shelf
zones.purpose: Hold the reference you genuinely reach for, at the height you reach for it from.
zones.done_looks_like: Working reference at seated eye level from the desk chair, heavy binders and box files on the bottom two shelves, a bookend closing each group, a hand's width of empty shelf left at the end of every row, and the unit screwed to the wall.

passes.sort: Take every book, binder, and manual off the shelves. Appliance manuals for machines that left the house, superseded editions with a year in the title, and binders from projects that finished all go out in one pass.
passes.straighten: Group by why you reach: working reference at eye level from where you sit, occasional reading at standing height, archive boxes highest, heavy binders lowest.
passes.shine: Dust from the top shelf down with a dry cloth, wipe the front edge of each shelf, and vacuum the top edges of the books themselves, which is where the dust in this room actually settles.
passes.safety: Screw the unit into the wall studs, and move the box files, binders, and any framed glass award off the high shelf that sits above where your head is when you are working.
passes.standardize: A bookend closes every group, and a hand's width of empty shelf stays at the end of each row. When a shelf has no slack left, that is the visible signal that a book has to leave, not that you need another shelf.
passes.sustain: When you finish a book or close out a project binder, it does not go back on the shelf by reflex. It gets the keep-or-go question at that moment, while the answer is still obvious.

the_call.title: The shelf that says who you used to be
the_call.text: The textbooks from a degree, the professional library from a job you left, the reference set that a website now answers better and faster. These are the hardest books in the house to release, because they stand for a version of you that you have not formally retired. The rule that settles it: ask when you last took it down since it arrived on this shelf, not whether you might one day. If you cannot name a specific occasion, and the book is one you could borrow or reorder inside a week, it is no longer reference, it is display, and it must now win a display slot in open competition with everything else on the shelf. Most of them will not. Appliance manuals are simpler: model still in the house, keep it; model gone, it goes today.

watch_for.question: Fall, cut, or crush
watch_for.text: An unanchored shelf unit standing above the desk chair, with the heaviest binders and box files loaded on the top shelf. Anchor the unit and put the weight low.

leave_behind.standard: Every shelf keeps a hand's width of empty space, and heavy binders and box files never live above head height.
leave_behind.trigger: When you finish a book or close out a project binder.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Dust falls, so clean this unit from the very top down. The place it actually settles is the two spots nobody looks at: the top of the tallest shelf and the top edges of the books themselves.

surfaces.surface: The very top of the unit
surfaces.method: Reach up with a dry microfiber cloth and clear the whole top surface first, because this is where the room's dust really gathers and it drops onto everything below when you disturb it. Use a step, never the desk chair, to get up there.

surfaces.surface: The top edges of the books and binders
surfaces.method: Tilt each book or binder out slightly and run the vacuum dusting brush along its top edge, then wipe the group with a dry cloth. This is the grit that a shelf wipe alone always leaves behind.

surfaces.surface: The shelf boards and their front edges
surfaces.method: Slide the books off a section at a time, wipe the board with neutral pH cleaner on a wrung-out cloth, and do the front edge where hands grab to pull a spine out. Dry each board before the books return.

surfaces.surface: The box files and framed glass award on the shelves
surfaces.method: Lift each box file and wipe its lid and sides, and clean the glass of any framed award with a dry cloth so no wet residue runs behind the frame.

surfaces.surface: The wall anchor point and strap
surfaces.method: Wipe the bracket or strap that ties the unit to the wall and clear the dust from around the fixing so you can actually see it while you work.

surfaces.surface: The floor and skirting behind and beneath the unit
surfaces.method: Vacuum along the bottom shelf, the skirting, and as far behind the unit as the crevice tool reaches, since this gap is where dust bunnies and dropped papers hide.

inspect_as_you_clean: As you clear a section, sight along the shelf board and flag any bow or sag under the weight of the binders sitting on it.
Check the wall anchor while you wipe it and flag a strap that has gone slack or a screw head that stands proud of the wall.
Give the unit a gentle nudge with an empty shelf and flag any wobble or lean away from the wall.
Feel the wall behind the top shelf and flag a damp or cold patch that could be softening the boards over time.

zones.time_note: mostly quick, though matching cartridges to printer model numbers takes longer than you would think
zones.purpose: Turn paper into files and files into paper, without hunting for either.
zones.done_looks_like: Paper in a bin directly beneath the printer with a min line and a max line drawn inside it, one spare cartridge in a labelled box beside it, a single scan tray with a to-do side and a done side, clear air behind the machine, and nothing sitting on the lid.

passes.sort: Keep only ink or toner that matches the model number on the printer currently plugged in. The half reams of odd paper, the letterhead with the old address, and the envelopes from two houses ago go out.
passes.straighten: Paper goes directly under the printer, the spare cartridge in a labelled box beside it, and the scan pile gets one tray with a to-do side and a done side, so you can tell at a glance what has already been through the glass.
passes.shine: Powered off, lift the lid and clean the scanner glass with cleaner on the cloth, never sprayed onto the glass where it can run inside. Use a dry cloth for toner dust and vacuum the paper lint around the feed tray.
passes.safety: Leave clear air at the back of the machine, because the fuser runs genuinely hot, and plug the printer straight into a wall outlet rather than into a strip chained off another strip. Nothing sits on top of the lid, not the plant and not your drink.
passes.standardize: Draw a min line and a max line inside the paper bin. When the stack drops to the min line, the next ream goes on the shopping list that day, not the day it runs out mid-job.
passes.sustain: When you pull the last sheet from the bin, refill it from the shelf before you walk away from the machine, while you are already standing there.

the_call.title: The backup printer
the_call.text: The old printer is still in the corner, or on the floor of the cupboard, because it might be a backup. Settle it before you leave this corner today: plug it in and print a test page right now. If it prints, and you are prepared to keep a spare cartridge for it in stock, it is a backup and it gets a home. If you will not plug it in today, it is not a backup, it is a large object you have not decided about, and it goes to electronics recycling this week. Apply the same blade to the sealed cartridges: hold each box against the model number on the machine you actually use. Anything unmatched sells this week for more than it will ever be worth again, because cartridge value only falls.

watch_for.question: Burn or fire
watch_for.text: A laser printer pushed tight against the wall or into a closed cupboard with no clearance behind it, and powered through a strip plugged into another strip. The fuser needs air and the machine needs its own wall outlet.

watch_for.question: Water and electricity
watch_for.text: A plant or a water glass sitting on top of the printer lid, directly above the electronics and the paper path.

leave_behind.standard: Only cartridges matching the printer on the desk are stocked, the paper bin carries a min line, and the top of the machine stays bare.
leave_behind.trigger: When you take the last sheet out of the paper bin.

shine_detail.shine_summary: Power off, then work from the glass down to the floor. The rule that saves the machine: cleaner goes onto the cloth, never onto the glass or into a vent, where it runs inside and finds the electronics.

surfaces.surface: The scanner glass under the lid
